## UI SURFACE MAP — Agent Display & Status

### 1. **THE DISPATCH LIST** (Agent Rows)

**Files:**

**What Each Agent Row Shows Today:**

| Element | Data Source | Line | Details |
|---------|------------|------|---------|
| **Index cell (color-coded)** | `dispatchActivityClasses()` | 426-479 | Fixed-width chip showing row label (A1, A2, ★1, etc). Background color = activity state |
| **Activity background colors** | `dispatchActivity()` → `runtime.streamPhase` + `runtime.sessionStatus` | 410-420 | `working` (green-600), `running` (blue-600), `starting` (orange-500), `exited` (red-700), `idle` (zinc-700) |
| **Title (main text)** | Latest user prompt OR session title | 228-229, 312-322 | Truncated with `.../` connector for linked agents; cached from `entries` |
| **Subtitle (row 2)** | `dispatchSubtitle()` derives from stream phase | 227, 324-347 | Shows: `thinking`, `responding`, `tool-input`, `tool-use`, `awaiting-tool`, `running`, `idle`, `exited`, `starting` |
| **Worktree badge** | `workContext` + `workActivity` | 289 | Visual indicator if agent is linked to a git/npm worktree |
| **Agent kind badge** | `row.kind` (claude/codex/terminal) | 291 | Text badge: "Claude" / "Codex" / "Terminal" |
| **Unread badge** | `unreadKind` ("attention" or "output") + `conditions` errors | 277-279, 349-357 | Amber "ACTION" or blue "NEW" pill when agent has unread output/actions |
| **Project chip (pinned rows only)** | `row.tabIndex` + `row.tabTitle` | 129, 292-303 | Shows project + tab letter for cross-project pinned agents |
| **Nesting indent (↳)** | `row.depth > 0` for linked/orchestration children | 259-266 | Visual connector for child agents under their parent |

**Visual Activity States (via `dispatchActivityClasses()` lines 425-479):**
- **Active**: Accent-colored index cell, selectable
- **Working**: Green-600 index (streamPhase ≠ 'idle')
- **Running**: Blue-600 index (sessionStatus = 'running')
- **Starting**: Orange-500 index (sessionStatus undefined)
- **Exited**: Red-700 index + dimmed text
- **Idle**: Zinc-700 index

**NOT shown per row:**
- Token usage (no count/spend field displayed)
- Runtime elapsed time (only in WorkIndicator inside the feed)
- Last tool called (only visible in the feed itself)
- Error message (only in Agent Status panel)
- Process/transcript readiness status (only in Agent Status panel)

---

### 2. **TILED DISPATCH MINI-LIST** (Compact Lane Selector)

**File:** `src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchMiniList.tsx`

**What It Shows:**
- **Index chips only** (lines 46-105): `[A1]` `[A2]` `[★1]` etc.
- **Activity-colored backgrounds** (line 84): Uses exact same palette as main list's index cells
- **Hover tooltip**: Prompt title (line 94)
- **Accent highlight**: Shows current lane's selected agent (line 50)

**Rationale (per comment lines 18-24):** "Rich context already lives one lane over in the full pinned index; repeating it here wastes the narrow column."

---

### 3. **TILED DISPATCH LAYOUT** (Multi-Lane Rendering)

**File:** `src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/TiledDispatchLayout.tsx`

**Structure (lines 155-264):**
- **Lane 0** (pinned index): Full DispatchAgentList (lines 163-178)
- **Lanes 1..N** (agent view): Each gets:
  - **Mini-list selector** (214-226): Compact chip strip (w-9 width)
  - **Splitter**: Draggable boundary to adjust lane weights (203-211)
  - **Agent view pane** (236-258): Full rendered Claude/Codex/Terminal view
  - **Unfocused scrim**: Translucent overlay (255-257) on non-focused lanes

**Focus affordance (line 227-250):**
- Only focused lane gets real `focusedSessionId` → accent border on TileLeaf
- Unfocused lanes render with 34% canvas scrim + border ring
- Clicking any unfocused lane auto-focuses it

---

### 4. **AGENT STATUS PANEL** (Per-Agent Inspector)

**File:** `src/renderer/src/features/agent-status/ui/AgentStatusPanel.tsx`

**Where It Lives:**
- Right-side drawer panel (390px width)
- Shown only when `openAgentStatusPanel` is true
- Triggered by command: "Show Agent Status"
- Toggle via `toggleAgentStatusPanel()`

**What It Displays (lines 78-98):**

| Section | Fields | Line | Source |
|---------|--------|------|--------|
| **Identity** | Session ID, Kind, Provider session, Cwd | 90, formatAgentStatus.ts:27-34 | `buildAgentStatusModel()` |
| **Runtime** | Session status, Process status, Transcript status, Activity | 91, formatAgentStatus.ts:36-58 | `runtime.*Status`, `streamPhase`, `activityStatus` |
| **Errors** (conditional) | Process error, Transcript error | 92, formatAgentStatus.ts:106-115 | `runtime.processError`, `runtime.transcriptError` |
| **Placement** | Placement bucket, Owner tab, Active tab?, Focused? | 93, formatAgentStatus.ts:60-67 | Dispatch row, grid owner, or detached entry |
| **Relationships** | Linked parent, Orch parent/root/run/role | 94, formatAgentStatus.ts:69-93 | `meta.linkedParentId`, `meta.orchestrationParentId`, etc. |
| **MCP** | Built-in MCP domains | 95, formatAgentStatus.ts:95-104 | `meta.builtInMcpDomains` |

**Header (lines 43-49):**
- Title: Session title or "No focused agent"
- Kind badge: "claude" / "codex" / "terminal"
- Close button

**Tone coloring (lines 137-142):**
- Good: green-400 (idle, ready)
- Warn: yellow-300 (running, spawning, loading)
- Bad: red-400 (failed, exited, error)

---

### 5. **LIVE PER-SESSION RUNTIME DATA AVAILABLE**

**File:** `src/renderer/src/workspace/workspaceState.ts` — `SessionRuntime` type (lines 278-526)

**Live Status Fields:**

| Field | Type | Updated | Usage |
|-------|------|---------|-------|
| `streamPhase` | 'idle' \| 'submitting' \| 'requesting' \| 'thinking' \| 'responding' \| 'tool-input' \| 'tool-use' \| 'awaiting-tool' | ✓ Live | Core "what is agent doing" — drives WorkIndicator, Dispatch subtitle, activity color |
| `streamPhasePendingToolName` | string \| null | ✓ Live | Tool name for tool-input/tool-use/awaiting-tool phases |
| `streamPhasePendingToolUseId` | string \| null | ✓ Live | Matched against tool_result to exit awaiting-tool |
| `sessionStatus` | 'idle' \| 'running' \| 'exited' | ✓ Live | Process-level readiness; second activity indicator |
| `sessionStatusSource` | 'none' \| 'submit' \| 'process' \| 'semantic' \| 'exit' | ✓ Live | Which subsystem set sessionStatus (debug/inspector only) |
| `processStatus` | 'idle' \| 'spawning' \| 'started' \| 'failed' \| 'exited' | ✓ Live | Backend PTY lifecycle; shown in Agent Status panel |
| `transcriptStatus` | 'idle' \| 'loading' \| 'ready' \| 'error' | ✓ Live | JSONL durability state; shown in Agent Status panel |
| `processError` | string \| null | ✓ Live | PTY spawn/exit error message; shown in Errors section of Agent Status |
| `transcriptError` | string \| null | ✓ Live | JSONL load failure; shown in Errors section of Agent Status |
| `activityStatus` | string \| null | ✓ Live | Compaction phase text (e.g., "compaction · 45%"); shown in Agent Status Activity field |
| `turnStartedAt` | number \| null | ✓ Live | Wall-clock ms when streamPhase left 'idle'; drives WorkIndicator elapsed timer |
| `phaseChangedAt` | number \| null | ✓ Live | Last phase transition time; for per-phase elapsed tracking |
| `submittedAt` | number \| null | ✓ Live | When user hit submit; WorkIndicator uses for 'submitting' phase start |
| `exited` | number \| null | ✓ Live | Unix timestamp when session ended (null = still running) |
| `entries` | Entry[] | ✓ Live (lazy-loaded) | Transcript history; used to extract latest user prompt for row title |
| `totalEntries` | number | ✓ Live | Total JSONL records on disk (for scroll indicator denominator) |
| `workContext` | AgentWorkContext \| null | ✓ Live | Git/npm context; renders WorktreeBadge in Dispatch rows |
| `workActivity` | WorktreeActivityState \| null | ✓ Live | Activity state for WorktreeBadge (idle/checking/cloning/etc) |
| `unreadSince` | number \| null | ✓ Live | When output became unread; shows 'output' badge |
| `unreadKind` | 'output' \| 'attention' \| null | ✓ Live | What kind of unread event (paired with conditions for 'attention') |
| `conditions` | ProviderConditionSnapshot \| null | ✓ Live | Provider state (rate limits, etc); drives "ACTION" attention label |
| `awaitingAssistant` | boolean | ✓ Live | Whether input is waiting for assistant (for gating) |
| `queuedMessages` | QueuedMessage[] | ✓ Live | Queued sends during rate-limit; not visually surfaced in list |
| `semantic` | SemanticRuntimeState | ✓ Live | Turn history + flow/error log; not shown in Dispatch list (only in Feed) |
| `ghosts` | Map<string, GhostEntry> | ✓ Live | Provisional entries while JSONL writes; Feed merges these |

**NOT available per-session (no "overview" fields):**
- Token usage (input/output spend) — stored in Turn/Entry semantic blocks, not aggregate
- Last assistant text — stored in entries, would require walk to extract
- Time since last activity — would require deriving from turnStartedAt vs. now
- Health/uptime metrics — not tracked at session level

---

### 6. **OVERVIEW/DASHBOARD SURFACES**

**Current State:**
- **NO dedicated overview/dashboard grid** showing all agents at once
- **Dispatch list** is the *only* multi-agent surface:
  - Classic Dispatch: Full index (list of rows grouped by tab)
  - Tiled Dispatch: Lane-0 index (same list) + N parallel views
- **Group header running count** (DispatchGroupHeader, line 164-171): `runningCount/{rows.length}` shows per-tab summary
  - Counts agents with `sessionStatus === 'running'` OR `streamPhase !== 'idle'`
  - Does NOT break down idle/working/running/exited individually

**Rationale for no dashboard:**
- Agent Code prioritizes "focus one agent deeply" over "scan all at once"
- Dispatch list already shows all live agents grouped by project
- Tiled Dispatch shows multiple agents side-by-side in parallel lanes
- Rich per-agent detail lives in Agent Status panel (drawer) for deep inspection

---

## HONEST GAPS — What Would Help "See All + Drill Into One"

### For "Active Agents at a Glance":

1. **No individual phase breakdown in group headers**
   - Group shows `runningCount/total` but not "2 thinking, 1 awaiting-tool, 3 idle"
   - Would need a multi-line summary or tooltip with phase distribution

2. **No session runtime elapsed time in Dispatch rows**
   - WorkIndicator shows elapsed only inside the focused pane's feed
   - Dispatch rows don't show "started 3m ago" or "running for 45s"

3. **No quick-scan token/cost meter**
   - Token usage is buried in semantic turns (Feed-only view)
   - No aggregate or per-session cost indicator in list context
   - Gap especially acute in Tiled Dispatch where agents run in parallel

4. **No heat map of activity intensity**
   - All non-idle agents render the same activity colors
   - "Which agent is most active?" requires reading subtitle + watching elapsed time
   - Could use saturation/brightness to show phase recency or phase intensity

5. **Activity color doesn't distinguish** "just finished" vs. "stuck in thinking for 2 hours"
   - All `working` agents are the same green-600
   - Would benefit from visual feedback on phase duration

6. **Dispatch list requires scrolling** at high agent counts
   - No pagination / no truncation with "+N more" affordance
   - No search/filter by agent name or status

### For "Drill Into One Agent":

1. **Agent Status panel doesn't show live updates to streamPhase/elapsed time**
   - Panel reads `buildAgentStatusModel()` once; doesn't tick with phaseChangedAt
   - Shows static snapshot, not live phase transitions
   - User must close/re-open or watch the Feed to see state changes

2. **No last assistant text / last tool output in Agent Status**
   - Operator can't see what the agent last said or last did without opening Feed
   - Gap for "status check" workflow: "What was it doing?"

3. **No "current tool details" in panel**
   - Shows tool name in streamPhasePendingToolName, but not tool arguments or partial results
   - User must go to Feed to see tool invocation details

4. **No error/exception context**
   - Process errors are one-liners
   - No stack trace, logs, or recovery suggestions
   - Gap for "diagnose stuck agent" workflow

5. **No action buttons from Inspector**
   - Can't interrupt/pause/kill agent from Agent Status panel
   - Must navigate to Feed or use keyboard commands
   - Gap for "quick fix" workflows

6. **Relationships section shows IDs only**
   - Orchestration parent/root are 12-char shortened IDs
   - No hover/click to navigate to related agent
   - Hard to trace agent hierarchies in complex orchestration runs

### For Tiled Dispatch Specifically:

1. **Mini-list (lane selector) doesn't show agent status**
   - Chips are index-label-only (A1, A2, ★1)
   - Can't tell which agents are working without glancing back at the index
   - Could show activity dot on chip or label color

2. **No "at a glance which lane is busiest"**
   - All lanes render equally; visual weight doesn't reflect agent state
   - Could dim unfocused idle agents or highlight lanes with working agents

3. **No async lane lifecycle feedback**
   - When a lane is auto-filled from the "heal effect," no feedback to user
   - Could show toast/pulse on lane change from heal

---

## CODE LOCATIONS SUMMARY

**Dispatch List Display:**
- Row rendering: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchAgentList.tsx:183-307`
- Row data shape: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/dispatchSelectors.ts:6-21`
- Activity logic: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchAgentList.tsx:410-479` (dispatchActivity, dispatchActivityClasses, dispatchActivityDotClass)
- Subtitle derivation: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchAgentList.tsx:324-347`
- Group header + running count: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchAgentList.tsx:156-181`

**Tiled Layout:**
- Structure & lane management: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/TiledDispatchLayout.tsx:63-264`
- Mini-list: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/dispatch/DispatchMiniList.tsx:33-106`

**Agent Status Panel:**
- UI wrapper: `/src/renderer/src/features/agent-status/ui/AgentStatusPanel.tsx:24-97`
- Formatter: `/src/renderer/src/features/agent-status/model/formatAgentStatus.ts`
- Model builder: `/src/renderer/src/features/agent-status/model/agentStatusModel.ts:59-105`

**Runtime Data:**
- SessionRuntime type: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/workspaceState.ts:278-526`
- StreamPhase type: `/src/renderer/src/workspace/workspaceState.ts:268-277`

**Can we see what they're doing?** — **No.** You see the `description` and then the final result when it lands. The live internal work isn't surfaced.

But here's the thing that makes this very buildable: **every subagent I spawn is being written to disk live, right now, and the app just doesn't read it.** Proof from your *current* session:

- `f074404f/subagents/agent-a6ec6f72d04aab973.jsonl` — 229 KB, written at **16:18:24** (that's the showcase-surfaces agent that just finished)
- 5+ sibling files, 200–340 KB each, mtimes tracking exactly when each agent was active

And the app has **no dedicated Task/Agent renderer at all** (grep for Task/subagent in the feed rows = nothing) — so those cards go through the generic path. The data exists; the wiring doesn't. Let me show you what's actually sitting in those files:

content.text:
**Found the linchpin.** The current meta.json carries exactly what makes this clean:

```json
{"agentType":"Explore","description":"Current active-agent showcase surfaces","toolUseId":"toolu_01KtyHpxD4nnXwuzUVBBCYS1"}
```

That `toolUseId` is a **direct, deterministic link** from each `subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` back to the exact `Task` card that spawned it. So the correlation problem I was fretting about earlier? **Solved on disk** — no wire heuristics, no guessing. And the file itself is the full story: that one agent did 42 turns / 25 tool calls (Bash, Read, Grep…), written live as it worked.

So everything we need exists and is reliable. **Yes — I now firmly suggest building this.** Here's the design.

## What we'd build

A real renderer for *your* spawned subagents, in two parts:

**1. Concurrency at a glance** — when I batch agents, group the sibling `Task` cards into one live header:
```
⏺ Spawned 4 agents    ◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done · 1m48s
  ├ ◐ Explore   "Render integration points for nested feed"    12 tools · 0:42
  ├ ◐ Explore   "Sub-agent flow correlation feasibility"        8 tools · 0:39
  ├ ✓ Explore   "Current active-agent showcase surfaces"       25 tools · done
  └ ✓ general   "Review agent-code PR #265"                     done
```

**2. Drill into any one** — expand a row to its live mini-feed (what it's doing *right now*):
```

# Subagent Fleet Rendering — Design Spec

- **Date:** 2026-06-14
- **Branch:** `feat/subagent-inline-render`
- **Status:** Design — awaiting user review before implementation plan
- **Author:** Agent Code (AI)

---

## 1. Problem

When the main agent spawns subagents via the `Task` tool — including several
**in parallel** (the common case: 4 `Explore` agents fired in one turn) — the
app renders each as a minimal, opaque card:

```
⏺ Task
  Current active-agent showcase surfaces
```

Two questions the operator cannot answer from the UI today:

1. **How many subagents are running at once?** When N `Task` blocks are spawned
   in one turn, you see N separate minimal cards with no concurrency summary,
   no "still running vs done" state, no elapsed time.
2. **What is each one doing?** You see only the `description` and, eventually,
   the final `tool_result`. The subagent's live internal work — its turns, its
   tool calls, its current activity — is invisible.

### Why this is worth building (and cheap to build correctly)

Everything we need is **already written to disk, live, and reliably linked** —
the app simply never reads it. Verified against the live session
`f074404f-.../subagents/` on 2026-06-14:

- Claude Code writes each subagent's **full transcript** to
  `<sessionDir>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, incrementally as the subagent
  works (file mtimes track activity in real time; sampled files were
  200–340 KB, dozens of turns each).
- Each transcript has a sidecar `agent-<id>.meta.json` carrying the
  **deterministic parent link**:

  ```json
  {"agentType":"Explore",
   "description":"Current active-agent showcase surfaces",
   "toolUseId":"toolu_01KtyHpxD4nnXwuzUVBBCYS1"}
  ```

  `toolUseId` matches the parent `Task` tool_use block's `id` exactly. **No
  heuristic correlation is required** — this is the fact that makes the whole
  feature robust. (Contrast: wire-level correlation via the proxy is
  impossible — every request gets a fresh `x-client-request-id` and the
  internal parent/child `chainId` never leaves the Claude Code process. Disk is
  the source of truth.)
- The subagent entries are standard Claude transcript shape
  (`type: user|assistant`, `message`, `uuid`, `parentUuid`, `isSidechain:true`),
  so the existing `agent-transcript-parser` can read them.

The app currently has **no dedicated renderer** for the `Task` tool at all
(`grep` for `Task`/`subagent` in `feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx` returns nothing — it
falls through to the generic `ToolUseRow`). So there is no existing behavior to
preserve or fight; we are filling a gap, not rewiring a contract.

---

## 2. Goals / Non-goals

### Goals

- **Concurrency at a glance.** Group sibling `Task` blocks spawned in one turn
  into a single live header: how many spawned, how many running, how many done,
  aggregate elapsed.
- **Drill into one.** Expand any subagent row to a **live mini-feed** of its
  tool-call timeline + a current-activity line, sourced from its
  `agent-<id>.jsonl`, updating live as the file grows.
- **Correct attribution.** Link each subagent to its parent `Task` card via
  `meta.toolUseId`. Never show a subagent under the wrong parent.
- **Durable.** Read from disk, so the view survives reload / re-focus, unlike
  the ephemeral proxy stream.

### Non-goals (YAGNI — explicitly out of scope for this PR)

- **No live proxy streaming** of subagent flows (fragile, uncorrelatable; disk
  is better).
- **No full-prose mini-feed by default.** The inline mini-feed shows the
  **tool-call timeline + current activity**, not the subagent's thinking/text.
  A "view full transcript" affordance is allowed as a thin escape hatch but the
  full transcript reader is not the focus.
- **No changes to the orchestration-MCP agents** (separate sessions / dispatch
  lanes — already streamed well, a different feature).
- **No Codex equivalent.** Codex does not spawn `Task` subagents this way; the
  feature is a no-op for Codex sessions.
- **No new persistent test suites** (per repo convention — temporary fixtures
  only; see §11).

---

## 3. Data model & linkage

### On-disk (source of truth, written by Claude Code)

```
<sessionDir>/
  <sessionId>.jsonl                  ← main transcript (already watched)
  subagents/
    agent-a6ec6f72d04aab973.jsonl    ← subagent full transcript (live-appended)
    agent-a6ec6f72d04aab973.meta.json← { agentType, description, toolUseId }
    agent-a156cda8c720cd845.jsonl
    agent-a156cda8c720cd845.meta.json
    ...
```

- **Parent link:** `meta.toolUseId` === the `Task` tool_use block `id` in the
  main transcript.
- **Liveness:** `agent-<id>.jsonl` is append-only and grows while the subagent
  runs. The file's last entry + the presence/absence of a matching
  `tool_result` in the parent transcript determine running-vs-done.

### Derived runtime state (new)

```ts
// One per spawned subagent, keyed by parent Task tool_use id.
type SubAgentState = {
  toolUseId: string            // links to the parent Task block (meta.toolUseId)
  agentId: string              // the agent-<id> filename id
  agentType: string            // meta.agentType, e.g. "Explore" | "general-purpose"
  description: string          // meta.description (the card headline)
  status: 'running' | 'done' | 'error'
  startedAt: number | null     // first entry ts
  lastActivityAt: number | null// last entry ts (drives elapsed + "live" pulse)
  turnCount: number            // assistant turns observed
  toolCalls: SubAgentToolCall[]// ordered tool-call timeline (capped, see §6)
  currentActivity: string | null // derived label: "running Grep", "thinking", …
}

type SubAgentToolCall = {
  name: string                 // "Read" | "Bash" | "Grep" | …
  headline: string | null      // first meaningful arg (path/command/pattern/query)
  status: 'running' | 'done'   // done once a tool_result for it appears
}
```

Stored on the per-session runtime:

```ts
// workspaceState.ts — SessionRuntime
subAgents: Record<string /* toolUseId */, SubAgentState>
```

Status is determined as:
- `running` — subagent file exists and the **parent** transcript has no
  `tool_result` block for this `toolUseId` yet.
- `done` — a `tool_result` for this `toolUseId` exists in the parent transcript.
- `error` — the `tool_result` is an error, or the file ends abnormally.

---

## 4. Architecture / data flow

```
 ┌─────────────────────────── main process ───────────────────────────┐
 │                                                                     │
 │  existing session-transcript watcher (sets transcriptStatus,        │
 │  streams entries for the main .jsonl)                               │
 │                          │                                          │
 │                          ├─ NEW: sibling watcher on subagents/      │
 │                          │     • on add/change of agent-<id>.jsonl  │
 │                          │       + meta.json                        │
 │                          │     • incremental parse via              │
 │                          │       agent-transcript-parser            │
 │                          │     • build/refresh SubAgentState        │
 │                          ▼                                          │
 │                   subAgentsForSession(sessionId): SubAgentState[]   │
 │                          │ IPC (same channel pattern as runtime)    │
 └──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
 ┌────────────────────── renderer ──────────────────────────────────┐
 │  SessionRuntime.subAgents: Record<toolUseId, SubAgentState>        │
 │                          │                                         │
 │  Feed render model: detect runs of sibling Task tool_use blocks    │
 │  → emit a "subagent group" render item                            │
 │                          │                                         │
 │  <SubAgentGroupRow>  (concurrency header)                          │
 │     └─ <SubAgentRow> × N  (per Task; looks up subAgents[block.id]) │
 │            └─ expanded: <SubAgentMiniFeed> (tool-call timeline)    │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Key principle: **the renderer never reads files.** It consumes
`runtime.subAgents` exactly like every other live field (`streamPhase`,
`ghosts`, …). All disk work is in the main process.

---

## 5. UI design (ASCII)

Status glyphs reuse the existing dispatch-activity vocabulary:
`◐` running (green), `✓` done, `✗` error (red), `⏸` queued.

### 5a. Collapsed — multiple subagents spawned in one turn (the common case)

The N sibling `Task` cards collapse into one live group header with per-agent
rows. Header shows the live tally + aggregate elapsed.

```
⏺ Spawned 4 agents              ◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done · 1m48s   [collapse ▾]
  ├ ◐ Explore   Render integration points for nested feed        12 tools · 0:42
  ├ ◐ Explore   Sub-agent flow correlation feasibility            8 tools · 0:39
  ├ ✓ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces           25 tools · done
  └ ✓ general   Review agent-code PR #265                              done
```

- Left glyph = per-subagent status (live).
- `agentType` shown dimmed before the description.
- Right column: live tool-call count + elapsed (running) or `done`.
- Each row is clickable to expand (§5c).

### 5b. Collapsed — a single subagent (degrades gracefully)

When only one `Task` is spawned, there is no group header — just the richer
single card:

```
⏺ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces      ◐ 12 tools · 0:42  [▸]
```

When done:

```
⏺ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces      ✓ 25 tools · 1m12s [▸]
```

### 5c. Expanded — drill into one subagent (the live mini-feed)

Expanding a row reveals its tool-call timeline + current-activity line, indented
under the row with a left rail. This is the "what is it doing right now" view.

```
  └ ▾ ◐ Explore  Render integration points for nested feed       12 tools · 0:42
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx
        ⏺ Grep   "tool_use"                                        18 matches
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/model/renderModel.ts
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../workspace/workspaceState.ts
        ◐ analyzing render model…                       ← current-activity line
        ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        view full transcript ▸                          ← thin escape hatch
```

When the subagent finishes, the current-activity line resolves and the card can
re-collapse to its `✓` summary; the final `tool_result` continues to render
where it already does (unchanged).

```
  └ ▾ ✓ Explore  Render integration points for nested feed       18 tools · 1m04s
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx
        …
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../workspace/workspaceState.ts
        ✓ returned — 6 integration points, 1 obstacle
        ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        view full transcript ▸
```

### 5d. Error / killed

```
  ├ ✗ Explore   Audit debug panel + PTY resolution        ✗ failed · 0:08
```

Expanding shows the partial timeline + the error reason from the `tool_result`.

### 5e. Live-update behavior

- The group header tally (`◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done`) and per-row tool counts /
  elapsed tick live as the watcher pushes state.
- Newly-appearing tool calls append to an expanded mini-feed in place (no
  scroll jump — append below, like the main feed's streaming).
- A subagent transitioning running→done flips its glyph and freezes its elapsed.

---

## 6. Bounds & performance

Subagent transcripts can be large (300 KB+, dozens of turns). Guardrails:

- **Incremental parse:** the watcher tracks a byte offset per `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  and parses only appended lines on each change (reuse the streaming parser
  approach already used for the main transcript). Never re-parse from zero.
- **Tool-call cap:** keep at most the last `SUBAGENT_TOOL_CALLS_MAX` (proposed
  **40**) tool calls in `toolCalls[]`, with a `… +N earlier` affordance. The
  mini-feed is a timeline, not a full log. `log()` the truncation count so it's
  not silently hidden.
- **Collapsed by default:** the mini-feed only mounts on expand (reuse the
  `LazyDetails` first-open lazy-mount idiom from `ToolResultRow.tsx`).
- **Per-session scoping:** the watcher runs only for the focused/active
  session(s) whose feed is mounted, not every session on disk.

---

## 7. Components & files

### Main process (all disk I/O here)

- **NEW** subagents watcher — locate the existing session-transcript watcher
  (the code that sets `transcriptStatus` / streams main `.jsonl` entries) and
  add a sibling watcher on `<sessionDir>/subagents/`. Emits `SubAgentState[]`
  per session over IPC.
- **REUSE** `packages/agent-transcript-parser` to parse `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  entries (tool_use extraction, turn counting).

### Renderer — state

- `workspace/workspaceState.ts` — add `subAgents: Record<string, SubAgentState>`
  to `SessionRuntime`; add `SubAgentState` / `SubAgentToolCall` types.
- IPC subscription wiring (the existing runtime-subscription hook) — fold
  pushed subagent state into `runtime.subAgents`.

### Renderer — feed model

- `features/feed/model/renderModel.ts` — detect a **run of sibling `Task`
  tool_use blocks** within an assistant turn and emit a single
  `type: 'subagent-group'` render item carrying the ordered `toolUseId`s. A lone
  `Task` emits a `subagent-single` (or the group renderer handles N=1).

### Renderer — components (new)

- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentGroupRow.tsx` — the concurrency header +
  the list of `SubAgentRow`s. Computes the live tally from `runtime.subAgents`.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentRow.tsx` — one subagent line; holds local
  `useState(expanded)`; renders `SubAgentMiniFeed` when open.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentMiniFeed.tsx` — the tool-call timeline +
  current-activity line; reuses `MarkerRow` and the `TruncatedOutputRow` collapse
  idiom; "view full transcript" escape hatch.

### Renderer — dispatch (Block.tsx)

- `features/feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx` — intercept `tool_use` blocks where
  `tu.name === 'Task'` **before** the generic `ToolUseRow` default, routing them
  into the subagent rendering path (or letting the render-model grouping handle
  them upstream — chosen during planning).

### Reused idioms (do not reinvent)

- Collapse / lazy-mount: `ToolResultRow.tsx` `LazyDetails`,
  `TruncatedOutputRow.tsx` (`useState(expanded)` + `… +N (click to expand)`).
- Status colors: `dispatch/DispatchAgentList.tsx` `dispatchActivity*`
  (green=working, blue=running, red=exited).
- Row layout: `MarkerRow` (`⏺` / `⎿` markers).

---

## 8. Edge cases & failure modes

- **`subagents/` dir absent** (no subagents spawned this session): watcher is a
  no-op; feed renders exactly as today. Zero regression.
- **meta.json missing / malformed** (older Claude Code, partial write): fall
  back to the file id as `agentId`, `agentType: 'agent'`,
  `description: ''`; do not crash. If `toolUseId` is absent we cannot link —
  render the subagent ungrouped under a generic "subagent" card rather than
  guessing a parent.
- **Reload mid-run:** state rebuilds from disk on watcher init; running agents
  resume ticking, done agents show their summary. Durable by construction.
- **Subagent killed / session exits:** last-known timeline freezes; status
  resolves to `error` if the parent `tool_result` is an error, else stays at the
  last observed state with a stale indicator.
- **Nested subagents** (a subagent spawns its own subagents): out of scope —
  Claude Code writes those under the subagent's own dir; we render one level.
  Note it in the spec so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for a bug.
- **Concurrent sessions** each with their own `subagents/`: keyed by session;
  no cross-talk (the `subAgents` map lives on each `SessionRuntime`).
- **Codex sessions:** no `subagents/` dir; feature inert.
- **Very large transcripts:** bounded per §6.

---

## 9. Open questions (resolve during planning, not blocking)

1. **Grouping boundary:** group strictly by sibling `Task` blocks *within one
   assistant turn*, or also coalesce `Task` blocks across adjacent turns in the
   same "burst"? Lean: within one turn (simplest, matches how the API batches).
2. **Status source of truth:** parent `tool_result` presence vs. a terminal
   marker in the subagent file. Lean: parent `tool_result` (authoritative for
   "the main agent considers it done").
3. **Watcher hosting:** extend the existing transcript watcher vs. a dedicated
   subagents watcher module. Lean: dedicated module, invoked alongside the
   existing one, for isolation/testability.

---

## 10. Rollout

Single PR on `feat/subagent-inline-render`. No setting/flag — this is strictly
additive rendering for data that is otherwise invisible, with a clean no-op when
no subagents exist. (If we want a kill-switch, a single
`showSubagentDetail` setting can gate the group renderer, defaulting on — decide
during planning.)

---

## 11. Testing

Per repo convention (no new persistent test files / no new `test:*` scripts in
feature PRs): validate manually against the live `subagents/` data already on
disk, plus a **temporary** throwaway fixture for the parser mapping
(`meta.toolUseId` → `Task` block; running/done transition) deleted before the PR
lands. Manual acceptance:

1. Fire 4 parallel `Task` agents → group header shows `◐ 4 running`, ticking.
2. Expand one → live tool-call timeline grows in place.
3. Agents complete → glyphs flip to `✓`, elapsed freezes, tally updates.
4. Reload the session → state rebuilds from disk, done agents summarized.
5. Session with no subagents → feed identical to today.

---

## 12. Summary

The data to answer "how many agents are running and what are they doing" is
already on disk, live, and deterministically linked to its parent `Task` card by
`meta.toolUseId`. This spec wires that disk truth into the runtime via a
main-process watcher and renders it as (a) a live concurrency header grouping
sibling `Task` blocks and (b) an expandable per-subagent tool-call mini-feed —
reusing existing collapse/marker/color idioms, touching no existing contract,
and degrading to today's behavior when no subagents exist.
```

- `error` — the `tool_result` is an error, or the file ends abnormally.

---

## 4. Architecture / data flow

```
 ┌─────────────────────────── main process ───────────────────────────┐
 │                                                                     │
 │  existing session-transcript watcher (sets transcriptStatus,        │
 │  streams entries for the main .jsonl)                               │
 │                          │                                          │
 │                          ├─ NEW: sibling watcher on subagents/      │
 │                          │     • on add/change of agent-<id>.jsonl  │
 │                          │       + meta.json                        │
 │                          │     • incremental parse via              │
 │                          │       agent-transcript-parser            │
 │                          │     • build/refresh SubAgentState        │
 │                          ▼                                          │
 │                   subAgentsForSession(sessionId): SubAgentState[]   │
 │                          │ IPC (same channel pattern as runtime)    │
 └──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
 ┌────────────────────── renderer ──────────────────────────────────┐
 │  SessionRuntime.subAgents: Record<toolUseId, SubAgentState>        │
 │                          │                                         │
 │  Feed render model: detect runs of sibling Task tool_use blocks    │
 │  → emit a "subagent group" render item                            │
 │                          │                                         │
 │  <SubAgentGroupRow>  (concurrency header)                          │
 │     └─ <SubAgentRow> × N  (per Task; looks up subAgents[block.id]) │
 │            └─ expanded: <SubAgentMiniFeed> (tool-call timeline)    │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Key principle: **the renderer never reads files.** It consumes
`runtime.subAgents` exactly like every other live field (`streamPhase`,
`ghosts`, …). All disk work is in the main process.

---

## 5. UI design (ASCII)

Status glyphs reuse the existing dispatch-activity vocabulary:
`◐` running (green), `✓` done, `✗` error (red), `⏸` queued.

### 5a. Collapsed — multiple subagents spawned in one turn (the common case)

The N sibling `Task` cards collapse into one live group header with per-agent
rows. Header shows the live tally + aggregate elapsed.

```
⏺ Spawned 4 agents              ◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done · 1m48s   [collapse ▾]
  ├ ◐ Explore   Render integration points for nested feed        12 tools · 0:42
  ├ ◐ Explore   Sub-agent flow correlation feasibility            8 tools · 0:39
  ├ ✓ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces           25 tools · done
  └ ✓ general   Review agent-code PR #265                              done
```

- Left glyph = per-subagent status (live).
- `agentType` shown dimmed before the description.
- Right column: live tool-call count + elapsed (running) or `done`.
- Each row is clickable to expand (§5c).

### 5b. Collapsed — a single subagent (degrades gracefully)

When only one `Task` is spawned, there is no group header — just the richer
single card:

```
⏺ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces      ◐ 12 tools · 0:42  [▸]
```

When done:

```
⏺ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces      ✓ 25 tools · 1m12s [▸]
```

### 5c. Expanded — drill into one subagent (the live mini-feed)

Expanding a row reveals its tool-call timeline + current-activity line, indented
under the row with a left rail. This is the "what is it doing right now" view.

```
  └ ▾ ◐ Explore  Render integration points for nested feed       12 tools · 0:42
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx
        ⏺ Grep   "tool_use"                                        18 matches
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/model/renderModel.ts
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../workspace/workspaceState.ts
        ◐ analyzing render model…                       ← current-activity line
        ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        view full transcript ▸                          ← thin escape hatch
```

When the subagent finishes, the current-activity line resolves and the card can
re-collapse to its `✓` summary; the final `tool_result` continues to render
where it already does (unchanged).

```
  └ ▾ ✓ Explore  Render integration points for nested feed       18 tools · 1m04s
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx
        …
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../workspace/workspaceState.ts
        ✓ returned — 6 integration points, 1 obstacle
        ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        view full transcript ▸
```

### 5d. Error / killed

```
  ├ ✗ Explore   Audit debug panel + PTY resolution        ✗ failed · 0:08
```

Expanding shows the partial timeline + the error reason from the `tool_result`.

### 5e. Live-update behavior

- The group header tally (`◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done`) and per-row tool counts /
  elapsed tick live as the watcher pushes state.
- Newly-appearing tool calls append to an expanded mini-feed in place (no
  scroll jump — append below, like the main feed's streaming).
- A subagent transitioning running→done flips its glyph and freezes its elapsed.

---

## 6. Bounds & performance

Subagent transcripts can be large (300 KB+, dozens of turns). Guardrails:

- **Incremental parse:** the watcher tracks a byte offset per `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  and parses only appended lines on each change (reuse the streaming parser
  approach already used for the main transcript). Never re-parse from zero.
- **Tool-call cap:** keep at most the last `SUBAGENT_TOOL_CALLS_MAX` (proposed
  **40**) tool calls in `toolCalls[]`, with a `… +N earlier` affordance. The
  mini-feed is a timeline, not a full log. `log()` the truncation count so it's
  not silently hidden.
- **Collapsed by default:** the mini-feed only mounts on expand (reuse the
  `LazyDetails` first-open lazy-mount idiom from `ToolResultRow.tsx`).
- **Per-session scoping:** the watcher runs only for the focused/active
  session(s) whose feed is mounted, not every session on disk.

---

## 7. Components & files

### Main process (all disk I/O here)

- **NEW** subagents watcher — locate the existing session-transcript watcher
  (the code that sets `transcriptStatus` / streams main `.jsonl` entries) and
  add a sibling watcher on `<sessionDir>/subagents/`. Emits `SubAgentState[]`
  per session over IPC.
- **REUSE** `packages/agent-transcript-parser` to parse `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  entries (tool_use extraction, turn counting).

### Renderer — state

- `workspace/workspaceState.ts` — add `subAgents: Record<string, SubAgentState>`
  to `SessionRuntime`; add `SubAgentState` / `SubAgentToolCall` types.
- IPC subscription wiring (the existing runtime-subscription hook) — fold
  pushed subagent state into `runtime.subAgents`.

### Renderer — feed model

- `features/feed/model/renderModel.ts` — detect a **run of sibling `Task`
  tool_use blocks** within an assistant turn and emit a single
  `type: 'subagent-group'` render item carrying the ordered `toolUseId`s. A lone
  `Task` emits a `subagent-single` (or the group renderer handles N=1).

### Renderer — components (new)

- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentGroupRow.tsx` — the concurrency header +
  the list of `SubAgentRow`s. Computes the live tally from `runtime.subAgents`.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentRow.tsx` — one subagent line; holds local
  `useState(expanded)`; renders `SubAgentMiniFeed` when open.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentMiniFeed.tsx` — the tool-call timeline +
  current-activity line; reuses `MarkerRow` and the `TruncatedOutputRow` collapse
  idiom; "view full transcript" escape hatch.

### Renderer — dispatch (Block.tsx)

- `features/feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx` — intercept `tool_use` blocks where
  `tu.name === 'Task'` **before** the generic `ToolUseRow` default, routing them
  into the subagent rendering path (or letting the render-model grouping handle
  them upstream — chosen during planning).

### Reused idioms (do not reinvent)

- Collapse / lazy-mount: `ToolResultRow.tsx` `LazyDetails`,
  `TruncatedOutputRow.tsx` (`useState(expanded)` + `… +N (click to expand)`).
- Status colors: `dispatch/DispatchAgentList.tsx` `dispatchActivity*`
  (green=working, blue=running, red=exited).
- Row layout: `MarkerRow` (`⏺` / `⎿` markers).

---

## 8. Edge cases & failure modes

- **`subagents/` dir absent** (no subagents spawned this session): watcher is a
  no-op; feed renders exactly as today. Zero regression.
- **meta.json missing / malformed** (older Claude Code, partial write): fall
  back to the file id as `agentId`, `agentType: 'agent'`,
  `description: ''`; do not crash. If `toolUseId` is absent we cannot link —
  render the subagent ungrouped under a generic "subagent" card rather than
  guessing a parent.
- **Reload mid-run:** state rebuilds from disk on watcher init; running agents
  resume ticking, done agents show their summary. Durable by construction.
- **Subagent killed / session exits:** last-known timeline freezes; status
  resolves to `error` if the parent `tool_result` is an error, else stays at the
  last observed state with a stale indicator.
- **Nested subagents** (a subagent spawns its own subagents): out of scope —
  Claude Code writes those under the subagent's own dir; we render one level.
  Note it in the spec so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for a bug.
- **Concurrent sessions** each with their own `subagents/`: keyed by session;
  no cross-talk (the `subAgents` map lives on each `SessionRuntime`).
- **Codex sessions:** no `subagents/` dir; feature inert.
- **Very large transcripts:** bounded per §6.

---

## 9. Open questions (resolve during planning, not blocking)

1. **Grouping boundary:** group strictly by sibling `Task` blocks *within one
   assistant turn*, or also coalesce `Task` blocks across adjacent turns in the
   same "burst"? Lean: within one turn (simplest, matches how the API batches).
2. **Status source of truth:** parent `tool_result` presence vs. a terminal
   marker in the subagent file. Lean: parent `tool_result` (authoritative for
   "the main agent considers it done").
3. **Watcher hosting:** extend the existing transcript watcher vs. a dedicated
   subagents watcher module. Lean: dedicated module, invoked alongside the
   existing one, for isolation/testability.

---

## 10. Rollout

Single PR on `feat/subagent-inline-render`. No setting/flag — this is strictly
additive rendering for data that is otherwise invisible, with a clean no-op when
no subagents exist. (If we want a kill-switch, a single
`showSubagentDetail` setting can gate the group renderer, defaulting on — decide
during planning.)

---

## 11. Testing

Per repo convention (no new persistent test files / no new `test:*` scripts in
feature PRs): validate manually against the live `subagents/` data already on
disk, plus a **temporary** throwaway fixture for the parser mapping
(`meta.toolUseId` → `Task` block; running/done transition) deleted before the PR
lands. Manual acceptance:

1. Fire 4 parallel `Task` agents → group header shows `◐ 4 running`, ticking.
2. Expand one → live tool-call timeline grows in place.
3. Agents complete → glyphs flip to `✓`, elapsed freezes, tally updates.
4. Reload the session → state rebuilds from disk, done agents summarized.
5. Session with no subagents → feed identical to today.

---

## 12. Summary

The data to answer "how many agents are running and what are they doing" is
already on disk, live, and deterministically linked to its parent `Task` card by
`meta.toolUseId`. This spec wires that disk truth into the runtime via a
main-process watcher and renders it as (a) a live concurrency header grouping
sibling `Task` blocks and (b) an expandable per-subagent tool-call mini-feed —
reusing existing collapse/marker/color idioms, touching no existing contract,
and degrading to today's behavior when no subagents exist.
```

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

export async function readJsonlFile<T>(filePath: string): Promise<T[]> {
  const text = await readFile(filePath, 'utf8')
  return text
    .split('\n')
    .map(line => line.trim())
    .filter(line => line.length > 0)
    .map(line => JSON.parse(line) as T)
}
```
The main process reads JSONL files line-by-line, parses each JSON object, and passes the array to `toClaude()` or `toCodex()`. No streaming/incremental parsing—entire JSONL loaded into memory first.

  tool_use_id: string
  content: string | Array<{ type: string; text?: string; [k: string]: unknown }>
  is_error?: boolean

export function parseToolInput(raw: string): unknown {

  } catch {

const { text, metadata, richContent } = normalizeOutput(payload.output)
const isError =
  metadata && typeof metadata.exit_code === 'number' && metadata.exit_code !== 0

// lines 921-936: Build tool_result block

  type: 'tool_result',
  tool_use_id: payload.call_id,     // Links to original tool_use id

**ANSWER: NO streaming/incremental API. Whole-file only.**

```

**Known limitation documented in `docs/ghost.md`:**

The library does support an **append-only ghost log pattern** for streaming scenarios, but it's not a streaming parser — it's a *reconciliation layer* for multiple producers:

```typescript
// src/ghost.ts:2-24 (design notes)
// "A streaming ingestion pipeline (speech-to-text, external tool output)
//  folding signals into a transcript before an authoritative writer sees them."

**Ghost append-only JSONL works like this:**
1. Writer appends `createGhost(...)` records to a ghost log as content streams in
2. Reader calls `reduceGhostLog(ghostLines)` to get current state (last-write-wins per uuid)
3. When authoritative record arrives, append `supersedeGhost(...)` to mark it superseded
4. On export, ghosts are **skipped** by both converters (ghosts never reach durable transcripts)

**Actual streaming workaround used in codebase:** None documented. The main process uses the simple whole-file approach: read entire JSONL into memory, pass array to converter.

Checked. Here's the honest finding on **how we track subagents today**:

- The only existing handling of subagents is the `isSidechain` flag — and it's used purely to **skip** them (so a subagent's transcript doesn't show up as a separate top-level session in the session list). `sessionList.ts:178`, `SessionList.ts:176`. There is **no tracking of subagent internals** anywhere, and the headless package does **not** watch the `subagents/` dir.
- BUT you're right that we *do* already track the important part **for free**: every `Task` spawn is a `tool_use` block and its completion is a `tool_result` block — **both already stream into `runtime.entries`**, and there are already in-memory indices keyed by `tool_use_id` (`ToolUseIndexContext` / `ToolResultIndexContext`).

So we can split this cleanly, and the cheap half needs **zero** new machinery (and definitely no screen parsing):

**Tier 1 — from data we already track (no watcher, no IPC, no new main-process code):**
```
⏺ Spawned 4 agents          ◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done
  ├ ◐ Explore   Render integration points for nested feed
  ├ ◐ Explore   Sub-agent flow correlation feasibility
  ├ ✓ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces
  └ ✓ general   Review agent-code PR #265
```
Pure renderer work: read the `Task` blocks + whether a `tool_result` exists yet (running vs done) straight from the entries/indices we already have. Answers **"how many running"** + identity + status.

**Tier 2 — the live "what is each *doing*" timeline:**
```
  └ ▾ ◐ Explore  Render integration points…    12 tools · 0:42
        ⏺ Read  Block.tsx
        ⏺ Grep  "tool_use"        18 matches
        ◐ analyzing render model…
```
This is the *only* part that needs reading `subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`. To be precise: that's **reading JSONL files on disk** (exactly the kind of thing we already do for the main transcript) — **not** screen parsing. It's a modest file-tail watcher, but it *is* new main-process code.

So the real question is scope:

- **Tier 1 only** — ship the concurrency/status view built entirely on existing tracking, no new infra. Cheapest, lowest risk.
- **Tier 1 + Tier 2** — also get the live internal tool-timeline (the literal "what are they doing"), which requires the small disk watcher.

My read of your original ask ("can we see what they're doing?") points to **Tier 1 + Tier 2** — but Tier 2 is the new code you're wary of. Which do you want? If Tier 1 is enough for now, I'll rip the watcher out of the plan and build purely on the entries we already stream.

**Found the linchpin.** The current meta.json carries exactly what makes this clean:

```json
{"agentType":"Explore","description":"Current active-agent showcase surfaces","toolUseId":"toolu_01KtyHpxD4nnXwuzUVBBCYS1"}
```

That `toolUseId` is a **direct, deterministic link** from each `subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` back to the exact `Task` card that spawned it. So the correlation problem I was fretting about earlier? **Solved on disk** — no wire heuristics, no guessing. And the file itself is the full story: that one agent did 42 turns / 25 tool calls (Bash, Read, Grep…), written live as it worked.

So everything we need exists and is reliable. **Yes — I now firmly suggest building this.** Here's the design.

## What we'd build

A real renderer for *your* spawned subagents, in two parts:

**1. Concurrency at a glance** — when I batch agents, group the sibling `Task` cards into one live header:
```
⏺ Spawned 4 agents    ◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done · 1m48s
  ├ ◐ Explore   "Render integration points for nested feed"    12 tools · 0:42
  ├ ◐ Explore   "Sub-agent flow correlation feasibility"        8 tools · 0:39
  ├ ✓ Explore   "Current active-agent showcase surfaces"       25 tools · done
  └ ✓ general   "Review agent-code PR #265"                     done
```

**2. Drill into any one** — expand a row to its live mini-feed (what it's doing *right now*):
```
  └ ▾ ◐ Explore  "Render integration points for nested feed"    12 tools · 0:42
        ⏺ Read  src/.../Block.tsx
        ⏺ Grep  "tool_use"              18 matches
        ⏺ Read  src/.../renderModel.ts
        ◐ analyzing render model…
```

## How it works (architecture)
- **Main process** watches `<sessionDir>/subagents/*.jsonl` + `.meta.json` for the active session, parses incrementally (reuse `agent-transcript-parser`), and emits per-subagent state keyed by `toolUseId`: `{agentType, description, status, turnCount, toolCalls[], lastActivity, elapsed}`.
- **Runtime** stores it on `SessionRuntime` as `subAgents: Record<toolUseId, SubAgentState>` (live-updated over IPC, same pattern as everything else).

## 1. Problem

When the main agent spawns subagents via the `Task` tool — including several
**in parallel** (the common case: 4 `Explore` agents fired in one turn) — the
app renders each as a minimal, opaque card:

```
⏺ Task
  Current active-agent showcase surfaces

Two questions the operator cannot answer from the UI today:

1. **How many subagents are running at once?** When N `Task` blocks are spawned

   no "still running vs done" state, no elapsed time.
2. **What is each one doing?** You see only the `description` and, eventually,
   the final `tool_result`. The subagent's live internal work — its turns, its
   tool calls, its current activity — is invisible.

the app simply never reads it. Verified against the live session
`f074404f-.../subagents/` on 2026-06-14:

- Claude Code writes each subagent's **full transcript** to

  works (file mtimes track activity in real time; sampled files were
  200–340 KB, dozens of turns each).

  **deterministic parent link**:

  ```json
  {"agentType":"Explore",
   "description":"Current active-agent showcase surfaces",
   "toolUseId":"toolu_01KtyHpxD4nnXwuzUVBBCYS1"}
  ```

  `toolUseId` matches the parent `Task` tool_use block's `id` exactly. **No
  heuristic correlation is required** — this is the fact that makes the whole
  feature robust. (Contrast: wire-level correlation via the proxy is
  impossible — every request gets a fresh `x-client-request-id` and the
  internal parent/child `chainId` never leaves the Claude Code process. Disk is
  the source of truth.)
- The subagent entries are standard Claude transcript shape
  (`type: user|assistant`, `message`, `uuid`, `parentUuid`, `isSidechain:true`),
  so the existing `agent-transcript-parser` can read them.

The app currently has **no dedicated renderer** for the `Task` tool at all
(`grep` for `Task`/`subagent` in `feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx` returns nothing — it
falls through to the generic `ToolUseRow`). So there is no existing behavior to
preserve or fight; we are filling a gap, not rewiring a contract.

---

## 2. Goals / Non-goals

### Goals

- **Concurrency at a glance.** Group sibling `Task` blocks spawned in one turn
  into a single live header: how many spawned, how many running, how many done,
  aggregate elapsed.
- **Drill into one.** Expand any subagent row to a **live mini-feed** of its
  tool-call timeline + a current-activity line, sourced from its
  `agent-<id>.jsonl`, updating live as the file grows.
- **Correct attribution.** Link each subagent to its parent `Task` card via
  `meta.toolUseId`. Never show a subagent under the wrong parent.
- **Durable.** Read from disk, so the view survives reload / re-focus, unlike
  the ephemeral proxy stream.

### Non-goals (YAGNI — explicitly out of scope for this PR)

- **No live proxy streaming** of subagent flows (fragile, uncorrelatable; disk
  is better).
- **No full-prose mini-feed by default.** The inline mini-feed shows the
  **tool-call timeline + current activity**, not the subagent's thinking/text.
  A "view full transcript" affordance is allowed as a thin escape hatch but the
  full transcript reader is not the focus.
- **No changes to the orchestration-MCP agents** (separate sessions / dispatch
  lanes — already streamed well, a different feature).
- **No Codex equivalent.** Codex does not spawn `Task` subagents this way; the
  feature is a no-op for Codex sessions.
- **No new persistent test suites** (per repo convention — temporary fixtures
  only; see §11).

---

## 3. Data model & linkage

### On-disk (source of truth, written by Claude Code)

```
<sessionDir>/
  <sessionId>.jsonl                  ← main transcript (already watched)
  subagents/
    agent-a6ec6f72d04aab973.jsonl    ← subagent full transcript (live-appended)
    agent-a6ec6f72d04aab973.meta.json← { agentType, description, toolUseId }
    agent-a156cda8c720cd845.jsonl
    agent-a156cda8c720cd845.meta.json
    ...
```

- **Parent link:** `meta.toolUseId` === the `Task` tool_use block `id` in the
  main transcript.
- **Liveness:** `agent-<id>.jsonl` is append-only and grows while the subagent
  runs. The file's last entry + the presence/absence of a matching
  `tool_result` in the parent transcript determine running-vs-done.

### Derived runtime state (new)

```ts
// One per spawned subagent, keyed by parent Task tool_use id.
type SubAgentState = {
  toolUseId: string            // links to the parent Task block (meta.toolUseId)
  agentId: string              // the agent-<id> filename id
  agentType: string            // meta.agentType, e.g. "Explore" | "general-purpose"
  description: string          // meta.description (the card headline)
  status: 'running' | 'done' | 'error'
  startedAt: number | null     // first entry ts
  lastActivityAt: number | null// last entry ts (drives elapsed + "live" pulse)
  turnCount: number            // assistant turns observed
  toolCalls: SubAgentToolCall[]// ordered tool-call timeline (capped, see §6)
  currentActivity: string | null // derived label: "running Grep", "thinking", …
}

type SubAgentToolCall = {
  name: string                 // "Read" | "Bash" | "Grep" | …
  headline: string | null      // first meaningful arg (path/command/pattern/query)
  status: 'running' | 'done'   // done once a tool_result for it appears
}
```

Stored on the per-session runtime:

```ts
// workspaceState.ts — SessionRuntime
subAgents: Record<string /* toolUseId */, SubAgentState>
```

Status is determined as:
- `running` — subagent file exists and the **parent** transcript has no
  `tool_result` block for this `toolUseId` yet.
- `done` — a `tool_result` for this `toolUseId` exists in the parent transcript.
- `error` — the `tool_result` is an error, or the file ends abnormally.

---

## 4. Architecture / data flow

```
 ┌─────────────────────────── main process ───────────────────────────┐
 │                                                                     │
 │  existing session-transcript watcher (sets transcriptStatus,        │
 │  streams entries for the main .jsonl)                               │
 │                          │                                          │
 │                          ├─ NEW: sibling watcher on subagents/      │
 │                          │     • on add/change of agent-<id>.jsonl  │
 │                          │       + meta.json                        │
 │                          │     • incremental parse via              │
 │                          │       agent-transcript-parser            │
 │                          │     • build/refresh SubAgentState        │
 │                          ▼                                          │
 │                   subAgentsForSession(sessionId): SubAgentState[]   │
 │                          │ IPC (same channel pattern as runtime)    │
 └──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
 ┌────────────────────── renderer ──────────────────────────────────┐
 │  SessionRuntime.subAgents: Record<toolUseId, SubAgentState>        │
 │                          │                                         │
 │  Feed render model: detect runs of sibling Task tool_use blocks    │
 │  → emit a "subagent group" render item                            │
 │                          │                                         │
 │  <SubAgentGroupRow>  (concurrency header)                          │
 │     └─ <SubAgentRow> × N  (per Task; looks up subAgents[block.id]) │
 │            └─ expanded: <SubAgentMiniFeed> (tool-call timeline)    │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Key principle: **the renderer never reads files.** It consumes
`runtime.subAgents` exactly like every other live field (`streamPhase`,
`ghosts`, …). All disk work is in the main process.

---

## 5. UI design (ASCII)

Status glyphs reuse the existing dispatch-activity vocabulary:
`◐` running (green), `✓` done, `✗` error (red), `⏸` queued.

### 5a. Collapsed — multiple subagents spawned in one turn (the common case)

The N sibling `Task` cards collapse into one live group header with per-agent
rows. Header shows the live tally + aggregate elapsed.

```
⏺ Spawned 4 agents              ◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done · 1m48s   [collapse ▾]
  ├ ◐ Explore   Render integration points for nested feed        12 tools · 0:42
  ├ ◐ Explore   Sub-agent flow correlation feasibility            8 tools · 0:39
  ├ ✓ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces           25 tools · done
  └ ✓ general   Review agent-code PR #265                              done
```

- Left glyph = per-subagent status (live).
- `agentType` shown dimmed before the description.
- Right column: live tool-call count + elapsed (running) or `done`.
- Each row is clickable to expand (§5c).

### 5b. Collapsed — a single subagent (degrades gracefully)

When only one `Task` is spawned, there is no group header — just the richer
single card:

```
⏺ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces      ◐ 12 tools · 0:42  [▸]
```

When done:

```
⏺ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces      ✓ 25 tools · 1m12s [▸]
```

### 5c. Expanded — drill into one subagent (the live mini-feed)

Expanding a row reveals its tool-call timeline + current-activity line, indented
under the row with a left rail. This is the "what is it doing right now" view.

```
  └ ▾ ◐ Explore  Render integration points for nested feed       12 tools · 0:42
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx
        ⏺ Grep   "tool_use"                                        18 matches
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/model/renderModel.ts
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../workspace/workspaceState.ts
        ◐ analyzing render model…                       ← current-activity line
        ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        view full transcript ▸                          ← thin escape hatch
```

When the subagent finishes, the current-activity line resolves and the card can
re-collapse to its `✓` summary; the final `tool_result` continues to render
where it already does (unchanged).

```
  └ ▾ ✓ Explore  Render integration points for nested feed       18 tools · 1m04s
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx
        …
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../workspace/workspaceState.ts
        ✓ returned — 6 integration points, 1 obstacle
        ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        view full transcript ▸
```

### 5d. Error / killed

```
  ├ ✗ Explore   Audit debug panel + PTY resolution        ✗ failed · 0:08
```

Expanding shows the partial timeline + the error reason from the `tool_result`.

### 5e. Live-update behavior

- The group header tally (`◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done`) and per-row tool counts /
  elapsed tick live as the watcher pushes state.
- Newly-appearing tool calls append to an expanded mini-feed in place (no
  scroll jump — append below, like the main feed's streaming).
- A subagent transitioning running→done flips its glyph and freezes its elapsed.

---

## 6. Bounds & performance

Subagent transcripts can be large (300 KB+, dozens of turns). Guardrails:

- **Incremental parse:** the watcher tracks a byte offset per `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  and parses only appended lines on each change (reuse the streaming parser
  approach already used for the main transcript). Never re-parse from zero.
- **Tool-call cap:** keep at most the last `SUBAGENT_TOOL_CALLS_MAX` (proposed
  **40**) tool calls in `toolCalls[]`, with a `… +N earlier` affordance. The
  mini-feed is a timeline, not a full log. `log()` the truncation count so it's
  not silently hidden.
- **Collapsed by default:** the mini-feed only mounts on expand (reuse the
  `LazyDetails` first-open lazy-mount idiom from `ToolResultRow.tsx`).
- **Per-session scoping:** the watcher runs only for the focused/active
  session(s) whose feed is mounted, not every session on disk.

---

## 7. Components & files

### Main process (all disk I/O here)

- **NEW** subagents watcher — locate the existing session-transcript watcher
  (the code that sets `transcriptStatus` / streams main `.jsonl` entries) and
  add a sibling watcher on `<sessionDir>/subagents/`. Emits `SubAgentState[]`
  per session over IPC.
- **REUSE** `packages/agent-transcript-parser` to parse `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  entries (tool_use extraction, turn counting).

### Renderer — state

- `workspace/workspaceState.ts` — add `subAgents: Record<string, SubAgentState>`
  to `SessionRuntime`; add `SubAgentState` / `SubAgentToolCall` types.
- IPC subscription wiring (the existing runtime-subscription hook) — fold
  pushed subagent state into `runtime.subAgents`.

### Renderer — feed model

- `features/feed/model/renderModel.ts` — detect a **run of sibling `Task`
  tool_use blocks** within an assistant turn and emit a single
  `type: 'subagent-group'` render item carrying the ordered `toolUseId`s. A lone
  `Task` emits a `subagent-single` (or the group renderer handles N=1).

### Renderer — components (new)

- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentGroupRow.tsx` — the concurrency header +
  the list of `SubAgentRow`s. Computes the live tally from `runtime.subAgents`.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentRow.tsx` — one subagent line; holds local
  `useState(expanded)`; renders `SubAgentMiniFeed` when open.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentMiniFeed.tsx` — the tool-call timeline +
  current-activity line; reuses `MarkerRow` and the `TruncatedOutputRow` collapse
  idiom; "view full transcript" escape hatch.

### Renderer — dispatch (Block.tsx)

- `features/feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx` — intercept `tool_use` blocks where
  `tu.name === 'Task'` **before** the generic `ToolUseRow` default, routing them
  into the subagent rendering path (or letting the render-model grouping handle
  them upstream — chosen during planning).

### Reused idioms (do not reinvent)

- Collapse / lazy-mount: `ToolResultRow.tsx` `LazyDetails`,
  `TruncatedOutputRow.tsx` (`useState(expanded)` + `… +N (click to expand)`).
- Status colors: `dispatch/DispatchAgentList.tsx` `dispatchActivity*`
  (green=working, blue=running, red=exited).
- Row layout: `MarkerRow` (`⏺` / `⎿` markers).

---

## 8. Edge cases & failure modes

- **`subagents/` dir absent** (no subagents spawned this session): watcher is a
  no-op; feed renders exactly as today. Zero regression.
- **meta.json missing / malformed** (older Claude Code, partial write): fall
  back to the file id as `agentId`, `agentType: 'agent'`,
  `description: ''`; do not crash. If `toolUseId` is absent we cannot link —
  render the subagent ungrouped under a generic "subagent" card rather than
  guessing a parent.
- **Reload mid-run:** state rebuilds from disk on watcher init; running agents
  resume ticking, done agents show their summary. Durable by construction.
- **Subagent killed / session exits:** last-known timeline freezes; status
  resolves to `error` if the parent `tool_result` is an error, else stays at the
  last observed state with a stale indicator.
- **Nested subagents** (a subagent spawns its own subagents): out of scope —
  Claude Code writes those under the subagent's own dir; we render one level.
  Note it in the spec so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for a bug.
- **Concurrent sessions** each with their own `subagents/`: keyed by session;
  no cross-talk (the `subAgents` map lives on each `SessionRuntime`).
- **Codex sessions:** no `subagents/` dir; feature inert.
- **Very large transcripts:** bounded per §6.

---

## 9. Open questions (resolve during planning, not blocking)

1. **Grouping boundary:** group strictly by sibling `Task` blocks *within one
   assistant turn*, or also coalesce `Task` blocks across adjacent turns in the
   same "burst"? Lean: within one turn (simplest, matches how the API batches).
2. **Status source of truth:** parent `tool_result` presence vs. a terminal
   marker in the subagent file. Lean: parent `tool_result` (authoritative for
   "the main agent considers it done").
3. **Watcher hosting:** extend the existing transcript watcher vs. a dedicated
   subagents watcher module. Lean: dedicated module, invoked alongside the
   existing one, for isolation/testability.

---

## 10. Rollout

Single PR on `feat/subagent-inline-render`. No setting/flag — this is strictly
additive rendering for data that is otherwise invisible, with a clean no-op when
no subagents exist. (If we want a kill-switch, a single
`showSubagentDetail` setting can gate the group renderer, defaulting on — decide
during planning.)

---

## 11. Testing

Per repo convention (no new persistent test files / no new `test:*` scripts in
feature PRs): validate manually against the live `subagents/` data already on
disk, plus a **temporary** throwaway fixture for the parser mapping
(`meta.toolUseId` → `Task` block; running/done transition) deleted before the PR
lands. Manual acceptance:

1. Fire 4 parallel `Task` agents → group header shows `◐ 4 running`, ticking.
2. Expand one → live tool-call timeline grows in place.
3. Agents complete → glyphs flip to `✓`, elapsed freezes, tally updates.
4. Reload the session → state rebuilds from disk, done agents summarized.
5. Session with no subagents → feed identical to today.

---

## 12. Summary

The data to answer "how many agents are running and what are they doing" is
already on disk, live, and deterministically linked to its parent `Task` card by
`meta.toolUseId`. This spec wires that disk truth into the runtime via a
main-process watcher and renders it as (a) a live concurrency header grouping
sibling `Task` blocks and (b) an expandable per-subagent tool-call mini-feed —
reusing existing collapse/marker/color idioms, touching no existing contract,
and degrading to today's behavior when no subagents exist.
```"}

## 3. Data model & linkage

### On-disk (source of truth, written by Claude Code)

```
<sessionDir>/
  <sessionId>.jsonl                  ← main transcript (already watched)
  subagents/
    agent-a6ec6f72d04aab973.jsonl    ← subagent full transcript (live-appended)
    agent-a6ec6f72d04aab973.meta.json← { agentType, description, toolUseId }
    agent-a156cda8c720cd845.jsonl
    agent-a156cda8c720cd845.meta.json
    ...
```

- **Parent link:** `meta.toolUseId` === the `Task` tool_use block `id` in the
  main transcript.
- **Liveness:** `agent-<id>.jsonl` is append-only and grows while the subagent
  runs. The file's last entry + the presence/absence of a matching
  `tool_result` in the parent transcript determine running-vs-done.

### Derived runtime state (new)

```ts
// One per spawned subagent, keyed by parent Task tool_use id.
type SubAgentState = {
  toolUseId: string            // links to the parent Task block (meta.toolUseId)
  agentId: string              // the agent-<id> filename id
  agentType: string            // meta.agentType, e.g. "Explore" | "general-purpose"
  description: string          // meta.description (the card headline)
  status: 'running' | 'done' | 'error'
  startedAt: number | null     // first entry ts
  lastActivityAt: number | null// last entry ts (drives elapsed + "live" pulse)
  turnCount: number            // assistant turns observed
  toolCalls: SubAgentToolCall[]// ordered tool-call timeline (capped, see §6)
  currentActivity: string | null // derived label: "running Grep", "thinking", …
}

type SubAgentToolCall = {
  name: string                 // "Read" | "Bash" | "Grep" | …
  headline: string | null      // first meaningful arg (path/command/pattern/query)
  status: 'running' | 'done'   // done once a tool_result for it appears
}
```

Stored on the per-session runtime:

```ts
// workspaceState.ts — SessionRuntime
subAgents: Record<string /* toolUseId */, SubAgentState>
```

Status is determined as:
- `running` — subagent file exists and the **parent** transcript has no
  `tool_result` block for this `toolUseId` yet.
- `done` — a `tool_result` for this `toolUseId` exists in the parent transcript.
- `error` — the `tool_result` is an error, or the file ends abnormally.
