## 5. UI design (ASCII)

Status glyphs reuse the existing dispatch-activity vocabulary:
`◐` running (green), `✓` done, `✗` error (red), `⏸` queued.

### 5a. Collapsed — multiple subagents spawned in one turn (the common case)

The N sibling `Task` cards collapse into one live group header with per-agent
rows. Header shows the live tally + aggregate elapsed.

```
⏺ Spawned 4 agents              ◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done · 1m48s   [collapse ▾]
  ├ ◐ Explore   Render integration points for nested feed        12 tools · 0:42
  ├ ◐ Explore   Sub-agent flow correlation feasibility            8 tools · 0:39
  ├ ✓ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces           25 tools · done
  └ ✓ general   Review agent-code PR #265                              done
```

- Left glyph = per-subagent status (live).
- `agentType` shown dimmed before the description.
- Right column: live tool-call count + elapsed (running) or `done`.
- Each row is clickable to expand (§5c).

### 5b. Collapsed — a single subagent (degrades gracefully)

When only one `Task` is spawned, there is no group header — just the richer
single card:

```
⏺ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces      ◐ 12 tools · 0:42  [▸]
```

When done:

```
⏺ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces      ✓ 25 tools · 1m12s [▸]
```

### 5c. Expanded — drill into one subagent (the live mini-feed)

Expanding a row reveals its tool-call timeline + current-activity line, indented
under the row with a left rail. This is the "what is it doing right now" view.

```
  └ ▾ ◐ Explore  Render integration points for nested feed       12 tools · 0:42
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx
        ⏺ Grep   "tool_use"                                        18 matches
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/model/renderModel.ts
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../workspace/workspaceState.ts
        ◐ analyzing render model…                       ← current-activity line
        ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        view full transcript ▸                          ← thin escape hatch
```

When the subagent finishes, the current-activity line resolves and the card can
re-collapse to its `✓` summary; the final `tool_result` continues to render
where it already does (unchanged).

```
  └ ▾ ✓ Explore  Render integration points for nested feed       18 tools · 1m04s
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx
        …
        ⏺ Read   src/renderer/.../workspace/workspaceState.ts
        ✓ returned — 6 integration points, 1 obstacle
        ────────────────────────────────────────────────
        view full transcript ▸

### 5d. Error / killed

```

```

Expanding shows the partial timeline + the error reason from the `tool_result`.

### 5e. Live-update behavior

- The group header tally (`◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done`) and per-row tool counts /
  elapsed tick live as the watcher pushes state.
- Newly-appearing tool calls append to an expanded mini-feed in place (no
  scroll jump — append below, like the main feed's streaming).
- A subagent transitioning running→done flips its glyph and freezes its elapsed.

## 6. Bounds & performance

Subagent transcripts can be large (300 KB+, dozens of turns). Guardrails:

- **Incremental parse:** the watcher tracks a byte offset per `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  and parses only appended lines on each change (reuse the streaming parser
  approach already used for the main transcript). Never re-parse from zero.
- **Tool-call cap:** keep at most the last `SUBAGENT_TOOL_CALLS_MAX` (proposed
  **40**) tool calls in `toolCalls[]`, with a `… +N earlier` affordance. The
  mini-feed is a timeline, not a full log. `log()` the truncation count so it's
  not silently hidden.
- **Collapsed by default:** the mini-feed only mounts on expand (reuse the
  `LazyDetails` first-open lazy-mount idiom from `ToolResultRow.tsx`).
- **Per-session scoping:** the watcher runs only for the focused/active
  session(s) whose feed is mounted, not every session on disk.

### Main process (all disk I/O here)

- **NEW** subagents watcher — locate the existing session-transcript watcher
  (the code that sets `transcriptStatus` / streams main `.jsonl` entries) and
  add a sibling watcher on `<sessionDir>/subagents/`. Emits `SubAgentState[]`
  per session over IPC.
- **REUSE** `packages/agent-transcript-parser` to parse `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  entries (tool_use extraction, turn counting).

### Renderer — state

- `workspace/workspaceState.ts` — add `subAgents: Record<string, SubAgentState>`
  to `SessionRuntime`; add `SubAgentState` / `SubAgentToolCall` types.

  pushed subagent state into `runtime.subAgents`.

### Renderer — feed model

- `features/feed/model/renderModel.ts` — detect a **run of sibling `Task`
  tool_use blocks** within an assistant turn and emit a single
  `type: 'subagent-group'` render item carrying the ordered `toolUseId`s. A lone
  `Task` emits a `subagent-single` (or the group renderer handles N=1).

### Renderer — components (new)

  the list of `SubAgentRow`s. Computes the live tally from `runtime.subAgents`.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentRow.tsx` — one subagent line; holds local
  `useState(expanded)`; renders `SubAgentMiniFeed` when open.

- `features/feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx` — intercept `tool_use` blocks where
  `tu.name === 'Task'` **before** the generic `ToolUseRow` default, routing them
  into the subagent rendering path (or letting the render-model grouping handle
  them upstream — chosen during planning).

### Reused idioms (do not reinvent)

- Collapse / lazy-mount: `ToolResultRow.tsx` `LazyDetails`,
  `TruncatedOutputRow.tsx` (`useState(expanded)` + `… +N (click to expand)`).

## 8. Edge cases & failure modes

- **`subagents/` dir absent** (no subagents spawned this session): watcher is a
  no-op; feed renders exactly as today. Zero regression.
- **meta.json missing / malformed** (older Claude Code, partial write): fall
  back to the file id as `agentId`, `agentType: 'agent'`,
  `description: ''`; do not crash. If `toolUseId` is absent we cannot link —
  render the subagent ungrouped under a generic "subagent" card rather than
  guessing a parent.
- **Reload mid-run:** state rebuilds from disk on watcher init; running agents
  resume ticking, done agents show their summary. Durable by construction.
- **Subagent killed / session exits:** last-known timeline freezes; status
  resolves to `error` if the parent `tool_result` is an error, else stays at the
  last observed state with a stale indicator.
- **Nested subagents** (a subagent spawns its own subagents): out of scope —
  Claude Code writes those under the subagent's own dir; we render one level.
  Note it in the spec so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for a bug.
- **Concurrent sessions** each with their own `subagents/`: keyed by session;
  no cross-talk (the `subAgents` map lives on each `SessionRuntime`).
- **Codex sessions:** no `subagents/` dir; feature inert.
- **Very large transcripts:** bounded per §6.

## 9. Open questions (resolve during planning, not blocking)

1. **Grouping boundary:** group strictly by sibling `Task` blocks *within one
   assistant turn*, or also coalesce `Task` blocks across adjacent turns in the
   same "burst"? Lean: within one turn (simplest, matches how the API batches).
2. **Status source of truth:** parent `tool_result` presence vs. a terminal
   marker in the subagent file. Lean: parent `tool_result` (authoritative for
   "the main agent considers it done").
3. **Watcher hosting:** extend the existing transcript watcher vs. a dedicated
   subagents watcher module. Lean: dedicated module, invoked alongside the
   existing one, for isolation/testability.

## 1. Problem

When the main agent spawns subagents via the `Task` tool — including several
**in parallel** (the common case: 4 `Explore` agents fired in one turn) — the
app renders each as a minimal, opaque card:

```
⏺ Task
  Current active-agent showcase surfaces
```

Two questions the operator cannot answer from the UI today:

1. **How many subagents are running at once?** When N `Task` blocks are spawned
   in one turn, you see N separate minimal cards with no concurrency summary,
   no "still running vs done" state, no elapsed time.
2. **What is each one doing?** You see only the `description` and, eventually,
   the final `tool_result`. The subagent's live internal work — its turns, its
   tool calls, its current activity — is invisible.

### Why this is worth building (and cheap to build correctly)

Everything we need is **already written to disk, live, and reliably linked** —
the app simply never reads it. Verified against the live session
`f074404f-.../subagents/` on 2026-06-14:

- Claude Code writes each subagent's **full transcript** to
  `<sessionDir>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, incrementally as the subagent
  works (file mtimes track activity in real time; sampled files were
  200–340 KB, dozens of turns each).
- Each transcript has a sidecar `agent-<id>.meta.json` carrying the
  **deterministic parent link**:

  ```json
  {"agentType":"Explore",
   "description":"Current active-agent showcase surfaces",
   "toolUseId":"toolu_01KtyHpxD4nnXwuzUVBBCYS1"}
  ```

  `toolUseId` matches the parent `Task` tool_use block's `id` exactly. **No
  heuristic correlation is required** — this is the fact that makes the whole
  feature robust. (Contrast: wire-level correlation via the proxy is
  impossible — every request gets a fresh `x-client-request-id` and the
  internal parent/child `chainId` never leaves the Claude Code process. Disk is
  the source of truth.)
- The subagent entries are standard Claude transcript shape
  (`type: user|assistant`, `message`, `uuid`, `parentUuid`, `isSidechain:true`),
  so the existing `agent-transcript-parser` can read them.

The app currently has **no dedicated renderer** for the `Task` tool at all
(`grep` for `Task`/`subagent` in `feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx` returns nothing — it
falls through to the generic `ToolUseRow`). So there is no existing behavior to
preserve or fight; we are filling a gap, not rewiring a contract.

---

## 2. Goals / Non-goals

### Goals

- **Concurrency at a glance.** Group sibling `Task` blocks spawned in one turn
  into a single live header: how many spawned, how many running, how many done,
  aggregate elapsed.
- **Drill into one.** Expand any subagent row to a **live mini-feed** of its
  tool-call timeline + a current-activity line, sourced from its
  `agent-<id>.jsonl`, updating live as the file grows.
- **Correct attribution.** Link each subagent to its parent `Task` card via
  `meta.toolUseId`. Never show a subagent under the wrong parent.
- **Durable.** Read from disk, so the view survives reload / re-focus, unlike
  the ephemeral proxy stream.

### Non-goals (YAGNI — explicitly out of scope for this PR)

- **No live proxy streaming** of subagent flows (fragile, uncorrelatable; disk
  is better).
- **No full-prose mini-feed by default.** The inline mini-feed shows the
  **tool-call timeline + current activity**, not the subagent's thinking/text.
  A "view full transcript" affordance is allowed as a thin escape hatch but the
  full transcript reader is not the focus.
- **No changes to the orchestration-MCP agents** (separate sessions / dispatch
  lanes — already streamed well, a different feature).
- **No Codex equivalent.** Codex does not spawn `Task` subagents this way; the
  feature is a no-op for Codex sessions.
- **No new persistent test suites** (per repo convention — temporary fixtures
  only; see §11).

- **Per-session scoping:** the watcher runs only for the focused/active
  session(s) whose feed is mounted, not every session on disk.

---

## 7. Components & files

### Main process (all disk I/O here)

- **NEW** subagents watcher — locate the existing session-transcript watcher
  (the code that sets `transcriptStatus` / streams main `.jsonl` entries) and
  add a sibling watcher on `<sessionDir>/subagents/`. Emits `SubAgentState[]`
  per session over IPC.
- **REUSE** `packages/agent-transcript-parser` to parse `agent-<id>.jsonl`
  entries (tool_use extraction, turn counting).

### Renderer — state

- `workspace/workspaceState.ts` — add `subAgents: Record<string, SubAgentState>`
  to `SessionRuntime`; add `SubAgentState` / `SubAgentToolCall` types.
- IPC subscription wiring (the existing runtime-subscription hook) — fold
  pushed subagent state into `runtime.subAgents`.

### Renderer — feed model

- `features/feed/model/renderModel.ts` — detect a **run of sibling `Task`
  tool_use blocks** within an assistant turn and emit a single
  `type: 'subagent-group'` render item carrying the ordered `toolUseId`s. A lone
  `Task` emits a `subagent-single` (or the group renderer handles N=1).

### Renderer — components (new)

- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentGroupRow.tsx` — the concurrency header +
  the list of `SubAgentRow`s. Computes the live tally from `runtime.subAgents`.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentRow.tsx` — one subagent line; holds local
  `useState(expanded)`; renders `SubAgentMiniFeed` when open.
- `features/feed/ui/rows/SubAgentMiniFeed.tsx` — the tool-call timeline +
  current-activity line; reuses `MarkerRow` and the `TruncatedOutputRow` collapse
  idiom; "view full transcript" escape hatch.

### Renderer — dispatch (Block.tsx)

- `features/feed/ui/rows/Block.tsx` — intercept `tool_use` blocks where
  `tu.name === 'Task'` **before** the generic `ToolUseRow` default, routing them
  into the subagent rendering path (or letting the render-model grouping handle
  them upstream — chosen during planning).

### Reused idioms (do not reinvent)

- Collapse / lazy-mount: `ToolResultRow.tsx` `LazyDetails`,
  `TruncatedOutputRow.tsx` (`useState(expanded)` + `… +N (click to expand)`).
- Status colors: `dispatch/DispatchAgentList.tsx` `dispatchActivity*`
  (green=working, blue=running, red=exited).
- Row layout: `MarkerRow` (`⏺` / `⎿` markers).

---

## 8. Edge cases & failure modes

- **`subagents/` dir absent** (no subagents spawned this session): watcher is a
  no-op; feed renders exactly as today. Zero regression.
- **meta.json missing / malformed** (older Claude Code, partial write): fall
  back to the file id as `agentId`, `agentType: 'agent'`,
  `description: ''`; do not crash. If `toolUseId` is absent we cannot link —
  render the subagent ungrouped under a generic "subagent" card rather than
  guessing a parent.
- **Reload mid-run:** state rebuilds from disk on watcher init; running agents
  resume ticking, done agents show their summary. Durable by construction.
- **Subagent killed / session exits:** last-known timeline freezes; status
  resolves to `error` if the parent `tool_result` is an error, else stays at the
  last observed state with a stale indicator.
- **Nested subagents** (a subagent spawns its own subagents): out of scope —
  Claude Code writes those under the subagent's own dir; we render one level.
  Note it in the spec so a future reader doesn't mistake the omission for a bug.
- **Concurrent sessions** each with their own `subagents/`: keyed by session;
  no cross-talk (the `subAgents` map lives on each `SessionRuntime`).
- **Codex sessions:** no `subagents/` dir; feature inert.
- **Very large transcripts:** bounded per §6.

---

## 9. Open questions (resolve during planning, not blocking)

1. **Grouping boundary:** group strictly by sibling `Task` blocks *within one
   assistant turn*, or also coalesce `Task` blocks across adjacent turns in the
   same "burst"? Lean: within one turn (simplest, matches how the API batches).
2. **Status source of truth:** parent `tool_result` presence vs. a terminal
   marker in the subagent file. Lean: parent `tool_result` (authoritative for
   "the main agent considers it done").
3. **Watcher hosting:** extend the existing transcript watcher vs. a dedicated
   subagents watcher module. Lean: dedicated module, invoked alongside the
   existing one, for isolation/testability.

---

## 10. Rollout

Single PR on `feat/subagent-inline-render`. No setting/flag — this is strictly
additive rendering for data that is otherwise invisible, with a clean no-op when
no subagents exist. (If we want a kill-switch, a single
`showSubagentDetail` setting can gate the group renderer, defaulting on — decide
during planning.)

---

## 11. Testing

Per repo convention (no new persistent test files / no new `test:*` scripts in
feature PRs): validate manually against the live `subagents/` data already on
disk, plus a **temporary** throwaway fixture for the parser mapping
(`meta.toolUseId` → `Task` block; running/done transition) deleted before the PR
lands. Manual acceptance:

1. Fire 4 parallel `Task` agents → group header shows `◐ 4 running`, ticking.
2. Expand one → live tool-call timeline grows in place.
3. Agents complete → glyphs flip to `✓`, elapsed freezes, tally updates.
4. Reload the session → state rebuilds from disk, done agents summarized.
5. Session with no subagents → feed identical to today.

---

## 12. Summary

The data to answer "how many agents are running and what are they doing" is
already on disk, live, and deterministically linked to its parent `Task` card by
`meta.toolUseId`. This spec wires that disk truth into the runtime via a
main-process watcher and renders it as (a) a live concurrency header grouping
sibling `Task` blocks and (b) an expandable per-subagent tool-call mini-feed —
reusing existing collapse/marker/color idioms, touching no existing contract,
and degrading to today's behavior when no subagents exist.

## Report: Main-Process Transcript Watching Machinery

Based on my thorough analysis of the codebase, here's the exact documentation of the existing transcript-watching machinery that mirrors the pattern for subagent watchingfile:

---

### 1. **JSONL Watching & Parsing (In `claude-code-headless` - not directly in Agent Code main)**

The JSONL file watching happens inside the imported `claude-code-headless` package. In Agent Code main:

**File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/.worktrees/subagent-inline-render/src/providers/claude/runtime/claudeSession.ts`

**Lines 407-412:** Event forwarding from headless → SessionManager:
```typescript
this.headless.on('jsonl-entry', (entry, file) =>
  this.emit('jsonl-entry', entry, file),
)
this.headless.on('jsonl-error', err =>
  this.emit('jsonl-error', err),
)
```

The headless package handles:
- File watching via internal watcher (likely byte-offset tracking for incremental reads)
- Parsing new JSONL entries as they append
- Emitting `'jsonl-entry'` event with `(entry: JsonlEntry, file: string)` payload
- Emitting `'jsonl-error'` on read failures

---

### 2. **Session Directory Path Resolution**

**File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/.worktrees/subagent-inline-render/src/shared/runtime/projectDir.ts`

**Lines 56-64:** Main path-resolution function:
```typescript
/**
 * Resolve a working directory to the on-disk directory CC uses to store
 * its session JSONL files for that cwd:
 *   ~/.claude/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/
 */
export async function getProjectDirForCwd(cwd: string): Promise<string> {
  const canonical = await canonicalizePath(cwd)
  return join(getProjectsDir(), sanitizePath(canonical))
}
```

**Lines 45-54:** Supporting functions:
```typescript
export function getClaudeConfigHomeDir(): string {
  return (process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(homedir(), '.claude')).normalize('NFC')
}

export function getProjectsDir(): string {
  return join(getClaudeConfigHomeDir(), 'projects')
}
```

**Path structure:** `~/.claude/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/<sessionId>.jsonl`

For your subagents use case: given a session, the directory containing the main `.jsonl` is:
```
~/.claude/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/  ← parent dir
  subagents/                          ← sibling of main .jsonl
    agent-<id>.jsonl
    agent-<id>.meta.json
```

---

### 3. **Event Flow from Session → SessionManager → IPC Forwarder**

**File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/.worktrees/subagent-inline-render/src/main/sessionManager.ts`

**Lines 419-426:** SessionManager re-emits jsonl events:
```typescript
session.on('jsonl-entry', (entry: JsonlEntry, file: string) => {
  this.markActivity(sessionId)
  this.emit('jsonl-entry', { sessionId, entry, file })
})
session.on('jsonl-error', (error: Error) => {
  this.markActivity(sessionId)
  this.emit('jsonl-error', { sessionId, error })
})
```

**ManagerEvents type (lines 55-57):**
```typescript
'jsonl-entry': [{ sessionId: string; entry: JsonlEntry; file: string }]
'jsonl-error': [{ sessionId: string; error: Error }]
```

---

### 4. **IPC Push to Renderer**

**File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/.worktrees/subagent-inline-render/src/main/sessions/forwarder.ts`

**Lines 20-48:** Session event forwarder (the bridge that sends to IPC):
```typescript
export function wireSessionForwarder(
  manager: SessionManager,
  lspManager: LspManager,
): void {
  manager.on('started', payload => sendToMainWindow('session:started', payload))
  manager.on('screen', payload => sendToMainWindow('session:screen', payload))
  
  // Bulk-only forwarding...
  manager.on('jsonl-entry', payload => {
    enqueueJsonl(payload.sessionId, payload.entry, payload.file)
  })
  manager.on('jsonl-error', ({ sessionId, error }) =>
    sendToMainWindow('session:jsonl-error', {
      sessionId,
      message: String(error.message ?? error),
    }),
  )
  // ... other events
}
```

**Jsonl Coalescer File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/.worktrees/subagent-inline-render/src/main/sessions/jsonlCoalescer.ts`

**Lines 38-48:** Bulk payload assembly and IPC send:
```typescript
function flushJsonlFor(sessionId: string): void {
  const pending = jsonlPending.get(sessionId)
  if (!pending || pending.entries.length === 0) return
  const payload = {
    sessionId,
    entries: pending.entries,
  }
  pending.entries = []
  pending.flushScheduled = false
  sendToMainWindow('session:jsonl-entries', payload)
}
```

**IPC Channels:**
- `'session:jsonl-entries'` — bulk payload: `{ sessionId: string; entries: Array<{ entry: JsonlEntry; file: string }> }`
- `'session:jsonl-error'` — error payload: `{ sessionId: string; message: string }`

**IPC Implementation (sendToMainWindow):**

**File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/.worktrees/subagent-inline-render/src/main/window/mainWindow.ts`

**Lines 65-69:**
```typescript
export function sendToMainWindow(channel: string, ...args: unknown[]): void {
  if (mainWindow && !mainWindow.isDestroyed()) {
    mainWindow.webContents.send(channel, ...args)
  }
}
```

---

### 5. **Watcher Lifecycle: Start & Stop**

**File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/.worktrees/subagent-inline-render/src/main/sessionManager.ts`

**START (lines 483-485):** On session spawn:
```typescript
try {
  const startStartedAt = performance.now()
  await session.start()
```

The `session.start()` call (from ClaudeSession or CodexSession) internally:
- Constructs ClaudeCodeHeadless instance
- Headless internally starts its JSONL watcher
- Emits initial `'started'` event when ready

**STOP (lines 898-956):** On session kill:
```typescript
async kill(sessionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const entry = this.sessions.get(sessionId)
  if (!entry) return false
  await entry.session.stop()  // ← stops headless, kills watcher
  // ... cleanup ...
  this.sessions.delete(sessionId)
  // ... delete buffers and cleanup ...
  return true
}
```

---

### 6. **Transcript Status Lifecycle (idle/loading/ready/error)**

**transcriptStatus is RENDERER-side only** — the main process doesn't push status; the renderer derives it from IPC events.

**File:** `/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/.worktrees/subagent-inline-render/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/ipc/useIpcSubscriptions.ts`

**Status transitions:**

1. **'error'** — **Lines 550-557:**
   ```typescript
   const offErr = window.api.onSessionJsonlError(({ sessionId, message }) => {
     updateRuntime(sessionId, {
       transcriptStatus: 'error',
       transcriptError: message,
     })
   })
   ```

2. **'ready'** — **Lines 1367-1368:**
   ```typescript
   transcriptStatus: 'ready',
   transcriptError: null,
   ```
   Emitted on every successful `session:jsonl-entries` bulk delivery (line 958).

3. **'loading'** (implicitly) — set on spawn (see `src/renderer/.../session.ts` line ~43):
   ```typescript
   transcriptStatus: hasProviderSession ? 'loading' : 'ready',
   ```

---

## Summary Table

| Aspect | Location | Key Code |
|--------|----------|----------|
| **File watching & parsing** | `claude-code-headless` (external package) | Byte-offset tracking, incremental JSONL parsing |
| **Session dir resolution** | `src/shared/runtime/projectDir.ts` lines 56-64 | `getProjectDirForCwd()` → `~/.claude/projects/<sanitized-cwd>/` |
| **Watcher start** | `src/providers/claude/runtime/claudeSession.ts` line 535 | `await this.headless.start()` |
| **Watcher stop** | `src/main/sessionManager.ts` line 901 | `await entry.session.stop()` |
| **Event re-emit** | `src/main/sessionManager.ts` lines 419-426 | SessionManager emits `'jsonl-entry'` & `'jsonl-error'` |
| **Bulk coalescer** | `src/main/sessions/jsonlCoalescer.ts` | `enqueueJsonl()` + `setImmediate()` + `flushJsonlFor()` |
| **IPC channels** | `src/main/sessions/forwarder.ts` lines 30-38 | `'session:jsonl-entries'` (bulk), `'session:jsonl-error'` |
| **IPC send mechanism** | `src/main/window/mainWindow.ts` lines 65-69 | `webContents.send(channel, payload)` |
| **Status emission** | `src/renderer/.../useIpcSubscriptions.ts` | Derived from IPC events, not pushed from main |

---

1. Use the same `getProjectDirForCwd()` to resolve session dir
2. Create a parallel watcher for `sessionDir/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` + `.meta.json`

## Public API Documentation: `agent-transcript-parser`

### 1. Main Exported Functions & Entry Points

**Import path:** `agent-transcript-parser` (TypeScript ESM module)

// src/index.ts:46-55
export {

---

### 2. How Main Process Uses This Parser

**Real usage from `src/main/providerSwitch/switchProvider.ts:40-97`:**

```typescript
// Line 48: Read JSONL file as array of parsed entries
const sourceEntries = await readJsonlFile<ClaudeEntry>(sourceFilePath)

// Lines 66-71: Convert Claude → Codex with options
const translated = toCodex(sanitizeClaudeEntriesForResume(sourceEntries), {
  lossy: false,
  dropClaudeBootstrap: true,
  sanitizeForResume: true,
  targetSessionId: randomUUID(),
})

// Line 96: Read Codex rollout lines
const sourceLines = await readJsonlFile<CodexRolloutLine>(sourceFilePath)

// Line 97: Convert Codex → Claude (fidelity mode)
const translated = toClaude(sourceLines, { lossy: false })
```

**Helper used for JSONL parsing (`src/main/providerSwitch/shared.ts:22-29`):**

```typescript
export async function readJsonlFile<T>(filePath: string): Promise<T[]> {
  const text = await readFile(filePath, 'utf8')
  return text
    .split('\n')
    .map(line => line.trim())
    .filter(line => line.length > 0)
    .map(line => JSON.parse(line) as T)
}
```
The main process reads JSONL files line-by-line, parses each JSON object, and passes the array to `toClaude()` or `toCodex()`. No streaming/incremental parsing—entire JSONL loaded into memory first.

---

### 3. Entry, Message, and Content Block Types

**Claude Entry (top-level transcript record):**

```typescript
// src/types.ts:163-204
export type ClaudeEntry = WithAtp<{
  type: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system' | 'attachment' | 'file-history-snapshot' | 'custom-title' | string
  uuid: string
  parentUuid: string | null
  sessionId: string
  timestamp: string // ISO-8601
  message?: ClaudeMessage
  // ... many optional fields (cwd, gitBranch, isSidechain, etc.)
}>
```

**Claude Message:**

```typescript
// src/types.ts:153-161
export type ClaudeMessage = {
  role: ClaudeRole  // 'user' | 'assistant'
  content: string | ClaudeContentBlock[]
  model?: string
  id?: string
  usage?: Record<string, unknown>
  stop_reason?: string | null
  stop_sequence?: string | null
}
```

**Content Block Types (union of all possible blocks in a message):**

```typescript
// src/types.ts:113-151
export type ClaudeTextBlock = { type: 'text'; text: string }

export type ClaudeToolUseBlock = {
  type: 'tool_use'
  id: string
  name: string
  input: unknown  // structured args (parsed JSON)
  caller?: { type?: string } & Record<string, unknown>
  codex?: Record<string, unknown>  // round-trip metadata from Codex
}

export type ClaudeToolResultBlock = {
  type: 'tool_result'
  tool_use_id: string
  content: string | Array<{ type: string; text?: string; [k: string]: unknown }>
  is_error?: boolean
  codex?: Record<string, unknown>  // exit_code, duration_seconds, etc.
}

export type ClaudeThinkingBlock = {
  type: 'thinking'
  thinking: string
  signature?: string  // server-generated, required for API resume
}

export type ClaudeContentBlock =
  | ClaudeTextBlock
  | ClaudeToolUseBlock
  | ClaudeToolResultBlock
  | ClaudeThinkingBlock
  | { type: string; [k: string]: unknown } // forward-compat
```

---

### 4. Extracting Tool Calls and Results

**Tool call extraction pattern (from `src/toClaude.ts:820-877`):**

```typescript
// Example: mapFunctionCall extracts Codex function_call into Claude tool_use
// line 825: Parse tool input arguments
const originalInput = parseToolInput(payload.arguments)

// line 859-866: Build tool_use block with name and input
const block: ClaudeToolUseBlock = {
  type: 'tool_use',
  id: payload.call_id,           // Matches tool_use_id in paired tool_result
  name: claudeToolName,           // 'Bash', 'web_search', etc.
  input: toBashInput(originalInput), // Structured args object
  ...(payload.namespace ? { codex: { namespace: payload.namespace } } : {}),
}
```

**Helper function to parse tool input args (`src/util.ts:57-63`):**

```typescript
export function parseToolInput(raw: string): unknown {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)  // Codex stores args as JSON string
  } catch {
    return { arguments: raw }  // Fallback for malformed JSON
  }
}
```

**Tool result extraction pattern (from `src/toClaude.ts:880-949`):**

```typescript
// Extract tool result block from Codex function_call_output
// lines 890-892: Normalize output and detect errors
const { text, metadata, richContent } = normalizeOutput(payload.output)
const isError =
  metadata && typeof metadata.exit_code === 'number' && metadata.exit_code !== 0

// lines 921-936: Build tool_result block
const block: ClaudeToolResultBlock = {
  type: 'tool_result',
  tool_use_id: payload.call_id,     // Links to original tool_use id
  content: isError ? text : richContent ?? text,  // Error results = text only
  ...(isError ? { is_error: true } : {}),       // Error flag
  ...(metadata ? { codex: { metadata } } : {}), // Preserved metadata
}
```

**Error detection:** Tool results carry `is_error: boolean` flag. Extracted from:
- `metadata.exit_code !== 0` (Codex shell/function calls)
- `block.is_error` field (if already present in source)

**Sample utility for output normalization (`src/util.ts:80-152`):**

```typescript
export function normalizeOutput(
  raw: unknown,
): {
  text: string
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>
  richContent?: Array<{ type: string; text?: string; [k: string]: unknown }>
}
```
Extracts text + metadata from Codex output (string, JSON-wrapped, or array). Preserves structured content (text, image, document, search_result blocks).

---

### 5. Incremental/Streaming Parsing Capability

**ANSWER: NO streaming/incremental API. Whole-file only.**

The public API functions **require the complete array as input:**

```typescript
toClaude(lines: readonly CodexRolloutLine[])  // Array required
toCodex(entries: readonly ClaudeEntry[])      // Array required
```

**Known limitation documented in `docs/ghost.md`:**

The library does support an **append-only ghost log pattern** for streaming scenarios, but it's not a streaming parser — it's a *reconciliation layer* for multiple producers:

```typescript
// src/ghost.ts:2-24 (design notes)
// "A streaming ingestion pipeline (speech-to-text, external tool output)
//  folding signals into a transcript before an authoritative writer sees them."
```

**Ghost append-only JSONL works like this:**
1. Writer appends `createGhost(...)` records to a ghost log as content streams in
2. Reader calls `reduceGhostLog(ghostLines)` to get current state (last-write-wins per uuid)
3. When authoritative record arrives, append `supersedeGhost(...)` to mark it superseded
4. On export, ghosts are **skipped** by both converters (ghosts never reach durable transcripts)

**Actual streaming workaround used in codebase:** None documented. The main process uses the simple whole-file approach: read entire JSONL into memory, pass array to converter.

---

### 6. Options for Conversion

**Type: `ConvertOptions` (`src/toClaude.ts:37-89`)**

```typescript
export type ConvertOptions = {
  /** Skip embedding _atp sidecars. Smaller files but round-trip fidelity lost. */
  lossy?: boolean

  /** Target Codex session id. Only used by toCodex. */
  targetSessionId?: string

  /** Drop Claude's bootstrap/housekeeping entries before writing Codex rollout.
   *  Only used by toCodex. */
  dropClaudeBootstrap?: boolean

  /** Strip one-shot history mutations from codex-origin sidecars.
   *  Only used by toCodex. Prevents resume re-applying old /rollback or /compact. */
  sanitizeForResume?: boolean
}
```

**Real-world usage example (switchProvider):**

```typescript
// Claude → Codex (line 66-71 of switchProvider.ts)
const translated = toCodex(sourceEntries, {
  lossy: false,                    // Keep sidecars for round-trip fidelity
  dropClaudeBootstrap: true,       // Strip system-reminder on provider switch
  sanitizeForResume: true,         // Strip stale history mutations
  targetSessionId: randomUUID(),   // Fresh session id per switch
})

// Codex → Claude (line 97)
const translated = toClaude(sourceLines, { lossy: false })
```

---

### 7. Sidecar (Round-Trip Metadata)

**Purpose:** Preserve lossless round-trip by stashing original record in `_atp` field.

**Type:**

```typescript
// src/types.ts:14-57
export const ATP_KEY = '_atp' as const

export type AtpSidecar =
  | { origin: 'claude'; source: ClaudeEntry | ClaudeEntry[] }
  | { origin: 'codex'; source: CodexRolloutLine | CodexRolloutLine[] }
  | { origin: 'synthesized' }  // Converter-emitted boilerplate
  | AtpGhostSidecar            // Ghost (provisional entry)
```

**Sidecar helpers (`src/sidecar.ts`):**

```typescript
// Attach sidecar to converted record
export function attachSidecar<T extends object>(
  record: T,
  origin: AtpSidecar['origin'],
  source: ClaudeEntry | CodexRolloutLine,
): WithAtp<T>

// Read sidecar from record (returns null if invalid/missing)
export function readSidecar(record: unknown): AtpSidecar | null

// Check if record is a ghost
export function isGhost(record: unknown): record is GhostEntry

// Remove sidecar (lossy mode)
export function stripSidecar<T extends WithAtp<object>>(record: T): T
```

**Round-trip guarantee:**

```typescript
// README.md (line 18-20)
toClaude(toCodex(claudeEntries))  // === claudeEntries
toCodex(toClaude(codexLines))     // === codexLines
```
When `lossy: false`, the reverse converter reads `_atp.source` and emits it byte-identical (short-circuit path in `toClaude` lines 391-406, `toCodex` lines 157-187).

---

### 8. Helper Functions for Analysis

**Turn/entry counting:** Not built-in. Count entries directly:

```typescript
const turns = entries.filter(e => e.type === 'user').length
const assistantTurns = entries.filter(e => e.type === 'assistant').length
```

**Tool call extraction helper:**

```typescript
function extractToolCalls(entry: ClaudeEntry) {
  if (entry.type !== 'assistant' || !entry.message) return []
  const content = entry.message.content
  if (typeof content === 'string') return []
  return content.filter(
    (block): block is ClaudeToolUseBlock => block.type === 'tool_use'
  )
}
```

**Tool result extraction:**

```typescript
function extractToolResults(entry: ClaudeEntry) {
  if (entry.type !== 'user' || !entry.message) return []
  const content = entry.message.content
  if (typeof content === 'string') return []
  return content.filter(
    (block): block is ClaudeToolResultBlock => block.type === 'tool_result'
  )
}
```

---

## Summary Table

| Aspect | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Main entry point** | `toClaude(CodexRolloutLine[], opts?)` → `ClaudeEntry[]`; `toCodex(ClaudeEntry[], opts?)` → `CodexRolloutLine[]` |
| **JSONL parsing** | Custom line-by-line split + JSON.parse in calling code; no built-in parser |
| **Streaming** | NO. Requires full array. Ghost log available for reconciliation but not streaming conversion. |
| **Tool use block** | `{ type: 'tool_use', id, name, input: unknown, codex?: {...} }` |
| **Tool result block** | `{ type: 'tool_result', tool_use_id, content, is_error?: boolean, codex?: {...} }` |
| **Extract tool_use input** | Access `block.input` directly (structured object). Parse from Codex string with `parseToolInput(json)`. |
| **Error detection** | `block.is_error` flag or `metadata.exit_code !== 0` in `codex` field. |
| **Round-trip mode** | Default: `lossy: false` preserves `_atp` sidecar with original record for byte-identical reverse. |
| **Sidecar** | `_atp: { origin: 'claude'|'codex', source: ... }` on converted records (skipped if `lossy: true`). |
| **Ghost support** | Append-only JSONL reconciliation via `createGhost()`, `updateGhost()`, `mergeWithUpstream()`. **Not for streaming parsing** — for multi-producer provisional entries. |
| **Known gaps** | No incremental/streaming conversion; whole file loaded into memory. |

export async function readJsonlFile<T>(filePath: string): Promise<T[]> {
  const text = await readFile(filePath, 'utf8')
  return text
    .split('\n')
    .map(line => line.trim())
    .filter(line => line.length > 0)
    .map(line => JSON.parse(line) as T)
}
```

### 4. Extracting Tool Calls and Results

**Tool call extraction pattern (from `src/toClaude.ts:820-877`):**

```typescript

**Helper function to parse tool input args (`src/util.ts:57-63`):**

```typescript
export function parseToolInput(raw: string): unknown {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(raw)  // Codex stores args as JSON string
  } catch {
    return { arguments: raw }  // Fallback for malformed JSON
  }
}
```

**Tool result extraction pattern (from `src/toClaude.ts:880-949`):**

```typescript
// Extract tool result block from Codex function_call_output
// lines 890-892: Normalize output and detect errors
const { text, metadata, richContent } = normalizeOutput(payload.output)
const isError =
  metadata && typeof metadata.exit_code === 'number' && metadata.exit_code !== 0

// lines 921-936: Build tool_result block
const block: ClaudeToolResultBlock = {
  type: 'tool_result',
  tool_use_id: payload.call_id,     // Links to original tool_use id
  content: isError ? text : richContent ?? text,  // Error results = text only
  ...(isError ? { is_error: true } : {}),       // Error flag
  ...(metadata ? { codex: { metadata } } : {}), // Preserved metadata

- `metadata.exit_code !== 0` (Codex shell/function calls)
- `block.is_error` field (if already present in source)

**Sample utility for output normalization (`src/util.ts:80-152`):**

```typescript
export function normalizeOutput(
  raw: unknown,
): {
  text: string
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>

### 5. Incremental/Streaming Parsing Capability

**ANSWER: NO streaming/incremental API. Whole-file only.**

The public API functions **require the complete array as input:**

```typescript
toClaude(lines: readonly CodexRolloutLine[])  // Array required
toCodex(entries: readonly ClaudeEntry[])      // Array required
```

**Known limitation documented in `docs/ghost.md`:**

The library does support an **append-only ghost log pattern** for streaming scenarios, but it's not a streaming parser — it's a *reconciliation layer* for multiple producers:

```typescript
// src/ghost.ts:2-24 (design notes)
// "A streaming ingestion pipeline (speech-to-text, external tool output)
//  folding signals into a transcript before an authoritative writer sees them."
```

**Ghost append-only JSONL works like this:**
1. Writer appends `createGhost(...)` records to a ghost log as content streams in
2. Reader calls `reduceGhostLog(ghostLines)` to get current state (last-write-wins per uuid)
3. When authoritative record arrives, append `supersedeGhost(...)` to mark it superseded
4. On export, ghosts are **skipped** by both converters (ghosts never reach durable transcripts)

**Actual streaming workaround used in codebase:** None documented. The main process uses the simple whole-file approach: read entire JSONL into memory, pass array to converter.

### 6. Options for Conversion

**Type: `ConvertOptions` (`src/toClaude.ts:37-89`)**

```typescript
export type ConvertOptions = {
  /** Skip embedding _atp sidecars. Smaller files but round-trip fidelity lost. */
  lossy?: boolean

  /** Target Codex session id. Only used by toCodex. */
  targetSessionId?: string

  /** Drop Claude's bootstrap/housekeeping entries before writing Codex rollout.
   *  Only used by toCodex. */
  dropClaudeBootstrap?: boolean

  /** Strip one-shot history mutations from codex-origin sidecars.
   *  Only used by toCodex. Prevents resume re-applying old /rollback or /compact. */
  sanitizeForResume?: boolean
}
```

```typescript

  lossy: false,                    // Keep sidecars for round-trip fidelity
  dropClaudeBootstrap: true,       // Strip system-reminder on provider switch
  sanitizeForResume: true,         // Strip stale history mutations
  targetSessionId: randomUUID(),   // Fresh session id per switch
})

// Codex → Claude (line 97)
const translated = toClaude(sourceLines, { lossy: false })
```

### 7. Sidecar (Round-Trip Metadata)

**Purpose:** Preserve lossless round-trip by stashing original record in `_atp` field.

**Type:**

```typescript
// src/types.ts:14-57
export const ATP_KEY = '_atp' as const

export type AtpSidecar =
  | { origin: 'claude'; source: ClaudeEntry | ClaudeEntry[] }
  | { origin: 'codex'; source: CodexRolloutLine | CodexRolloutLine[] }
  | { origin: 'synthesized' }  // Converter-emitted boilerplate
  | AtpGhostSidecar            // Ghost (provisional entry)
```

**Sidecar helpers (`src/sidecar.ts`):**

```typescript
// Attach sidecar to converted record
export function attachSidecar<T extends object>(
  record: T,
  origin: AtpSidecar['origin'],
  source: ClaudeEntry | CodexRolloutLine,
): WithAtp<T>

// Read sidecar from record (returns null if invalid/missing)
export function readSidecar(record: unknown): AtpSidecar | null

// Check if record is a ghost
export function isGhost(record: unknown): record is GhostEntry

// Remove sidecar (lossy mode)
export function stripSidecar<T extends WithAtp<object>>(record: T): T
```

**Round-trip guarantee:**

```typescript
// README.md (line 18-20)
toClaude(toCodex(claudeEntries))  // === claudeEntries
toCodex(toClaude(codexLines))     // === codexLines
```
When `lossy: false`, the reverse converter reads `_atp.source` and emits it byte-identical (short-circuit path in `toClaude` lines 391-406, `toCodex` lines 157-187).

---

### 8. Helper Functions for Analysis

**Turn/entry counting:** Not built-in. Count entries directly:

```typescript
const turns = entries.filter(e => e.type === 'user').length
const assistantTurns = entries.filter(e => e.type === 'assistant').length
```

**Tool call extraction helper:**

```typescript
function extractToolCalls(entry: ClaudeEntry) {
  if (entry.type !== 'assistant' || !entry.message) return []
  const content = entry.message.content
  if (typeof content === 'string') return []
  return content.filter(
    (block): block is ClaudeToolUseBlock => block.type === 'tool_use'
  )
}
```

**Tool result extraction:**

```typescript
function extractToolResults(entry: ClaudeEntry) {
  if (entry.type !== 'user' || !entry.message) return []
  const content = entry.message.content
  if (typeof content === 'string') return []
  return content.filter(
    (block): block is ClaudeToolResultBlock => block.type === 'tool_result'
  )
}
```

Checked. Here's the honest finding on **how we track subagents today**:

- The only existing handling of subagents is the `isSidechain` flag — and it's used purely to **skip** them (so a subagent's transcript doesn't show up as a separate top-level session in the session list). `sessionList.ts:178`, `SessionList.ts:176`. There is **no tracking of subagent internals** anywhere, and the headless package does **not** watch the `subagents/` dir.
- BUT you're right that we *do* already track the important part **for free**: every `Task` spawn is a `tool_use` block and its completion is a `tool_result` block — **both already stream into `runtime.entries`**, and there are already in-memory indices keyed by `tool_use_id` (`ToolUseIndexContext` / `ToolResultIndexContext`).

So we can split this cleanly, and the cheap half needs **zero** new machinery (and definitely no screen parsing):

**Tier 1 — from data we already track (no watcher, no IPC, no new main-process code):**
```
⏺ Spawned 4 agents          ◐ 2 running · ✓ 2 done
  ├ ◐ Explore   Render integration points for nested feed
  ├ ◐ Explore   Sub-agent flow correlation feasibility
  ├ ✓ Explore   Current active-agent showcase surfaces
  └ ✓ general   Review agent-code PR #265
```
Pure renderer work: read the `Task` blocks + whether a `tool_result` exists yet (running vs done) straight from the entries/indices we already have. Answers **"how many running"** + identity + status.

**Tier 2 — the live "what is each *doing*" timeline:**
```
  └ ▾ ◐ Explore  Render integration points…    12 tools · 0:42
        ⏺ Read  Block.tsx
        ⏺ Grep  "tool_use"        18 matches
        ◐ analyzing render model…
```
This is the *only* part that needs reading `subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`. To be precise: that's **reading JSONL files on disk** (exactly the kind of thing we already do for the main transcript) — **not** screen parsing. It's a modest file-tail watcher, but it *is* new main-process code.

So the real question is scope:

- **Tier 1 only** — ship the concurrency/status view built entirely on existing tracking, no new infra. Cheapest, lowest risk.
- **Tier 1 + Tier 2** — also get the live internal tool-timeline (the literal "what are they doing"), which requires the small disk watcher.

My read of your original ask ("can we see what they're doing?") points to **Tier 1 + Tier 2** — but Tier 2 is the new code you're wary of. Which do you want? If Tier 1 is enough for now, I'll rip the watcher out of the plan and build purely on the entries we already stream.
